The primary focus of this position is air quality compliance — tracking emissions, managing permits, preparing regulatory reports, and ensuring SM Energy meets its obligations across upstream operations. This analyst brings strong data fluency to that work, using modern tools to reduce manual effort, improve accuracy, and surface compliance risk proactively

The right candidate is an environmental compliance professional who is comfortable with data — someone who can write SQL, build a Power BI dashboard, automate a recurring calculation in Python, and use AI tools like Claude to accelerate analysis and documentation. They build team-level solutions independently and exercise good judgment about when to partner with IT.

This is an opportunity to define what environmental data management looks like at SM Energy. The person in this role will modernize how the Air Team operates — bringing analytical rigor and tool fluency to a compliance program that spans hundreds of regulated facilities across multiple states.

Essential Roles And Responsibilities

Compliance Data and Workflow Support

Serve as the Air Team’s primary business-side input on the design and configuration of a new centralized environmental compliance platform, ensuring it accurately reflects regulatory requirements and operational workflows.
Translate air compliance requirements — permit conditions, emissions calculation logic, reporting deadlines — into documented functional specifications that IT and implementation partners can act on.
Configure and maintain automated workflow tools (Power Automate, Python scripting, or equivalent) to streamline recurring compliance tasks including calculations, deadline notifications, and data validation.
Coordinate with IT on data integration between the compliance platform and SM Energy’s enterprise environment (Snowflake, Microsoft 365, operational data sources), providing business requirements and validating outputs.
Use AI tools (Claude, Claude Code) alongside Python and Excel to automate repetitive compliance tasks, accelerate data analysis, and draft documentation and regulatory correspondence.
Document data architecture, system workflows, data dictionaries, and calculation methodologies to support auditability, knowledge transfer, and ongoing system maintenance.
Coordinate with SM Energy’s IT and data management teams to communicate Air Team needs, validate data outputs, and support platform enhancements over time.

Data Analytics and Compliance Reporting

Develop and maintain dashboards and reports that provide the Environmental/ Air Team and leadership with real-time visibility into compliance status, emissions performance, permit thresholds, and program metrics.
Design and maintain rolling 12-month emissions tracking models to monitor threshold proximity across permitted facilities, supporting proactive identification of applicability triggers.
Maintain and QA/QC air emissions calculations for regulated emission sources.
Build and maintain a centralized permit compliance tracker that monitors renewal deadlines, deviation reporting, condition compliance status, and upcoming regulatory submission obligations across all operating areas.
Support annual GHG emissions inventory preparation for EPA's Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP), including Subpart W calculations, facility-level data aggregation, QA/QC review, and e-GGRT submission support.
Support the preparation of federal and state-level air quality compliance reports.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Program Support

Partner with Environmental/ air compliance team throughout system design and deployment to ensure the platform accurately reflects regulatory requirements and operational workflows.
Coordinate with external consultants on data exchange, calculation methodology review, and integration of consultant deliverables into the compliance platform.
Support the integration of acquired assets into SM Energy's compliance infrastructure, including data migration from legacy systems and reconciliation of historical permit and emissions records.
Assist with internal and external compliance audits by generating data extracts, producing summary reports, and packaging documentation from the new platform.
Identify and recommend workflow improvements, automation opportunities, and analytical enhancements that increase team efficiency and compliance visibility as the new platform matures.
All other duties and projects as assigned.

Professional Skills

Ability to translate regulatory compliance requirements into clear functional specifications, working collaboratively with IT and data management teams to bring solutions to life.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a track record of working with large, complex datasets and producing clear, reliable outputs in a high-stakes compliance environment.
High attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy where errors carry legal, financial, and regulatory consequences.
Able to manage multiple concurrent compliance obligations and analytical workstreams, with strong judgment about when to escalate and when to run independently.
Effective communicator capable of translating complex compliance data into clear summaries for operations personnel, leadership, and regulators.
Comfortable operating under ambiguity, including post-acquisition integration environments where data sources are varied and documentation is incomplete.

COMPUTER AND SOFTWARE APPLICATIONS

Required

Microsoft Office 365, with advanced proficiency in Excel.
Power BI for dashboard and report development, data model design, and scheduled refresh configuration.
SQL for querying, transforming, and validating data across relational databases and cloud data platforms.
Power Automate or equivalent workflow automation tools for recurring compliance tasks and notification workflows.
Snowflake or equivalent cloud-based data warehouse platform.
Claude and Claude Code — accelerating analysis, automating calculation documentation, and drafting regulatory correspondence and reporting narratives.

Strongly Preferred

Python — calculation automation, data transformation, and scripting recurring compliance tasks.
Familiarity with environmental management information systems (EMIS) as a power user or configurator — enough to inform requirements and validate system behavior.
Familiarity with Intelex ACTS or a comparable EMIS platform, as a user or administrator, to inform the design of the replacement system.
Experience with mobile field data collection tools (e.g., ProntoForms, PowerApps, or equivalent) and data integration patterns from field to system of record.
Experience with Alteryx, Azure Data Factory, or equivalent ETL/data integration tools.
Familiarity with EPA's GHGRP Electronic Reporting Tool (e-GGRT) or state emissions inventory submission portals (NMED AFS, TCEQ STEERS/CEDRI, Utah DAQ).

Job Description

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is scaling rapidly to meet global cloud and AI capacity demand. The Datacenter Design organization is expanding its technical program management capability to improve the speed, consistency, and predictability of data hall design delivery across Oracle’s global datacenter portfolio.

We are seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager – Data Hall Design
to drive complex, cross-functional infrastructure programs that support OCI capacity growth. This role will report to the Director of Technical Program Management for Data Hall Design and will operate as a senior individual contributor responsible for program execution, delivery governance, risk management, dependency tracking, process improvement, and stakeholder alignment.

Data Hall Design includes the physical infrastructure design workstreams required to prepare data halls for scalable OCI deployment, including structured cabling, fiber infrastructure, low-voltage systems, physical networking dependencies, construction handoffs, colocation readiness, and operational handoff milestones.

This is an individual contributor role with no direct people-management responsibilities. Success in this role requires technical depth, strong ownership, structured execution, executive-ready communication, and the ability to drive clarity across ambiguous, high-stakes infrastructure programs.

Responsibilities

Program Leadership and Governance

Drive planning and execution for complex Data Hall Design programs, including roadmaps, milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, and measurable outcomes.
Establish and maintain program mechanisms such as milestone reviews, dependency trackers, risk registers, executive updates, KPI dashboards, and escalation paths.
Translate OCI capacity priorities into clear execution plans that align design, construction, networking, colocation, operations, supply chain, vendor, and automation workstreams.
Prepare clear, concise updates for senior leaders, including delivery status, risks, trade-offs, mitigation plans, and decision recommendations.

Data Hall Design Delivery

Drive cross-functional execution across structured cabling, fiber infrastructure, low-voltage systems, physical networking dependencies, construction handoffs, colocation readiness, and operational handoff milestones.
Partner with design engineering teams to ensure deliverables support scalability, maintainability, performance, cost, deployment speed, and operational readiness.
Identify and resolve blockers that could impact design release dates, construction execution, network readiness, vendor delivery, colocation fit-out, or OCI capacity availability.
Maintain accurate program plans, schedules, dependency maps, decision records, and status reporting across assigned programs.

Process Excellence and Standardization

Drive adoption of standardized design processes, templates, review cadences, handoff checklists, exception tracking, and change-management mechanisms.
Use data, metrics, and operating reviews to improve schedule predictability, blocker resolution, design package readiness, and handoff quality.
Partner with tooling, workflow automation, dashboarding, and reporting teams to improve visibility, accountability, and execution performance.
Capture lessons learned and help improve repeatable program mechanisms across regions and design workstreams.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as a key execution partner across Datacenter Design, Physical Networking, Construction, Colocation, Capacity Planning, Supply Chain, Datacenter Operations, Infrastructure Delivery, vendors, and automation teams.
Align stakeholders around goals, owners, timelines, risks, trade-offs, and decision points.
Influence without direct authority to drive accountability, unblock execution, and maintain urgency across multiple organizations.
Communicate effectively with technical and business stakeholders at multiple levels, from detailed project reviews to senior leadership updates.

Minimum Qualifications

8+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, Infrastructure Program Management, Datacenter Delivery, Engineering Operations, Cloud Infrastructure, or a related field.
Proven experience driving large-scale, cross-functional technical or infrastructure programs across cloud infrastructure, hyperscale datacenters, physical networking, colocation, telecommunications, construction, or mission-critical facilities.
Strong understanding of infrastructure delivery lifecycles, including design, construction, colocation readiness, networking dependencies, implementation readiness, operational readiness, and handoff to delivery or operations teams.
Experience building and operating program mechanisms such as roadmaps, milestone plans, dependency trackers, risk registers, executive reporting, dashboards, and KPI-based performance tracking.
Demonstrated ability to manage ambiguity, assess risk, evaluate trade-offs, prioritize competing demands, and drive decisions across engineering, construction, operations, supply chain, vendor, and business stakeholders.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience using data to identify trends, isolate root causes, and drive process improvement.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing executive-ready updates and driving alignment across technical and business teams.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, Project Management, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related technical or quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with OCI, hyperscale cloud infrastructure, global datacenter delivery, data hall design, physical networking, structured cabling, fiber infrastructure, low-voltage systems, or colocation delivery.
Familiarity with datacenter design workflows, design documentation, construction handoffs, operational readiness processes, and tools such as AutoCAD, Revit/BIM, or equivalent systems.
Experience using program management platforms, workflow tools, dashboarding, reporting, data analysis, or automation tools to improve portfolio visibility and execution performance.
Experience driving standardization across global programs, including reference designs, change management, review processes, handoff mechanisms, and operational readiness frameworks.
Experience partnering with software, tooling, data, or automation teams to improve infrastructure delivery processes.
Experience working with vendors, colocation providers, regional delivery teams, and cross-functional engineering organizations.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager - Design & Construction
jobs.description:
The Senior Project Manager - Design & Construction is responsible for leading complex capital projects through planning, design, permitting, and construction. Typical projects may include but are not limited to ground-up development of new parks, new buildings or outdoor recreation facilities within existing parks, major renovations to existing facilities, park master plans, feasibility analysis of potential land acquisitions, or grant-funded infrastructure improvements.

Hiring Salary Range:
$93,000 - $129,000

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS (with Illustrative Examples Of Work)

Project planning, design, and contract management

Lead the planning, budgeting, design, permitting, bidding, and contracting of park development projects.
Prepare Requests for Proposals, evaluate responses, contract for and administer design, engineering, and other professional services in accordance with the Virginia Procurement Act and NOVA Parks policies and procedures. Professional services include architecture, civil engineering, landscape architecture, environmental consulting, aquatics design, economic and feasibility analysis, surveying, etc.
Manage consultant teams in the development of feasibility studies, design drawings, permit plans, special zoning and agency permits, and construction documents in coordination with capital and park operations staff.
Conduct research and provide creative direction for unique, innovative, and mission-driven park project design elements.
Apply for and administer grants and alternative financing opportunities for projects that require external funding sources.
Assist with evaluation of potential land acquisitions including appraisals, site assessments, environmental studies, feasibility analysis, and purchase options.
Lead public engagement processes for park planning efforts and develop outreach strategies to include a diverse population of park users.
Manage the bidding process including preparation of construction bid packages, solicit and evaluate bids from qualified contractors, negotiate terms, and prepare contract documents in accordance with the VPA and NOVA Parks policies and procedures.
Attend local and regional government and agency meetings on behalf of NOVA Parks.
Assist with the development of NOVA Parks’ five-year capital budget.
Occasionally attend NOVA Parks Board meetings to present projects as directed.

Lead NOVA Parks’ construction activities

Administer the construction of new park facilities and capital improvements in accordance with the approved Capital Budget.
Develop and manage detailed budgets and schedules from early planning phases through construction and project turnover
Monitor onsite construction activities, keep accurate activity logs, and prepare written reports.
Consult with architects, engineers, third-party inspectors, and contractors in the field on a continual basis.
Schedule and conduct periodic inspections, project meetings, and punch-list walk-throughs.
Inspect quality of work and ensure adherence to plans, specifications, contracts, state and local codes, and NOVA Parks standards.
Observe third-party testing procedures, review test results and inspection reports, and facilitate corrective actions as required.
Resolve conflicts and problems on site, including making on-site engineering/design decisions both independently and in consultation with the project team.
Review requests for information, change orders, and requisitions for payment.
Work closely with appropriate Park Operations personnel in the scheduling and execution of construction activities.
Coordinate and assemble project turnover package for transition of completed projects to park staff.
Ensure staff and contractor adherence to safety standards and fair and equitable employment practices.
Assist Planning Team with oversight of licensed, third-party construction activities on park lands.
Support and mentor team members in your field of discipline.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS (minimum)

Education: Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, architecture, landscape architecture, planning, construction management, or closely related field.

Physical: Non-manual and manual work with strength and dexterity necessary to perform all required tasks, including lifting, stooping, bending, and working in tiring and uncomfortable positions in office and outdoor settings; must be able to maneuver through construction sites and properties with rugged terrain.

Experience: Ten to fifteen years of related experience as a professional designer and project manager in land development, park planning, site engineering, or construction of capital projects; Virginia DPOR Licensure in civil engineering, landscape architecture, or architecture with experience working in Northern Virginia jurisdictions preferred; or any equivalent combination of education, training, and experience which provides:

Considerable knowledge of standard planning, architecture, engineering and construction administration practices and procedures, including permitting requirements and processes in NOVA Parks’ member jurisdictions.
Considerable ability to interpret and understand land development and construction plans including but not limited to land surveys, deeds of trust, easements, zoning applications, architectural, civil, landscape, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, E&S, and stormwater management plans.
Extensive knowledge of principles, methods, practices, and techniques in the construction industry.
Considerable knowledge of materials and equipment used in construction. Considerable ability to interpret and adhere to construction specifications and contract documents.
Considerable knowledge of local construction codes and permit procedures.
Considerable ability to ensure contractor adherence to NOVA Parks contracts and specifications.
Knowledge of personnel management principles and ability to effectively supervise and mentor staff.
Considerable ability to communicate clearly and effectively, with ability to prepare and present accurate reports and presentations in a group setting and manage public engagement.
Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with contractors, architects, engineers, and co-workers.
Considerable knowledge of planning, bidding, contracting, and procurement procedures in compliance with the Virginia Procurement Act.
Considerable ability to analyze facts and to exercise sound judgment in arriving at conclusions.
Ability to operate personal computer with knowledge of applicable software including Microsoft Office Suite, (Word, Excel, Outlook, and Power Point). Experience with LandF/X, AutoCAD, GIS, Adobe Creative Suite, Microsoft Project, Procore, Trimble, and other industry standard software platforms desired.
Knowledge of and ability in general drafting techniques.
Possession of or ability to obtain Responsible Land Disturber certification with Virginia DEQ or equivalent is preferred.
Possession of or ability to obtain and maintain a VA driver's license with safe driving record.
Regular and predictable attendance is an essential function of the position.

Duties and responsibilities are designed to be the essential elements of the job. They do not preclude the performance of related, or even unrelated, jobs which may be necessary to properly and efficiently complete all work assignments. NOVA Parks reserves the right to amend job specifications to meet current needs.

Benefits:
This position is a benefit eligible position. Benefits include medical and dental insurance, life insurance, long-term disability, retirement plan, and more. This role is eligible to receive an annual bonus calculated as a percentage of the company’s net revenue. Distribution, timing, and metrics are discretionary and subject to individual and business performance.

Testing:
The Senior Project Manager position is classified as a safety sensitive position. Candidates for full-time, safety sensitive positions must submit to a pre-employment drug screening and achieve a negative result as a condition of employment.

jobs.description:
About The Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. Safely delivering increasingly capable AI systems requires scalable technical safeguards, clear ownership of emerging risks, rigorous deployment readiness, and close coordination across research, engineering, product, operations, legal, policy, and external partners.

Our Technical Program Managers lead complex, high-stakes initiatives that turn safety commitments into deployed systems and measurable outcomes. We work across model development, infrastructure, product, and operational response to help ensure our technology is deployed responsibly and cannot be used to cause serious real-world harm.

About The Role

We’re seeking Technical Program Managers to drive complex product, platform, and safety initiatives across ChatGPT, API, enterprise, and related deployment environments. These roles operate at the intersection of technical strategy and execution: you will turn safety and product priorities into actionable plans, influence architectural and operational decisions, and deliver durable capabilities across model, infrastructure, application, and platform layers.

Depending on the role, you may enable sensitive or high-impact model deployments, integrate safeguards into cloud and API platforms, prevent violent misuse and other serious harms, improve detection and enforcement systems, create platform solutions for safety or establish new programs as risks evolve. You will partner deeply with engineers, researchers, product managers, and operational teams while communicating technical tradeoffs and program decisions to senior leadership.

You bring technical fluency, product judgment, and a strong execution record. You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity, advocating for users and developers, balancing safety with model usefulness, and leading cross-functional work with urgency, rigor, and empathy. Specific focus areas and scope will vary by opening and level.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In This Role, You Will

Partner with product, engineering, research, and design to shape technical roadmaps, long-term platform direction, and safeguards priorities across ChatGPT, API, enterprise, and cloud environments.
Translate product and safety objectives into execution plans that balance near-term delivery, long-term platform evolution, customer needs, and responsible deployment.
Lead cross-functional programs end to end—from problem definition and technical design through implementation, launch, iteration, and operational follow-through.
Own milestones, dependencies, risk mitigation, decision-making, and accountability across engineering, infrastructure, integrity, trust and safety, legal, policy, operations, and go-to-market teams.
Partner with engineers on system architecture, public and internal APIs, cloud deployment patterns, platform integrations, operational failure modes, and technical tradeoffs.
Drive the development, integration, or rollout of safeguards such as model evaluations, post-training mitigations, classifiers, abuse detection, monitoring, enforcement workflows, human review, and agent-assisted review.
Coordinate readiness for sensitive or high-impact deployments, ensuring appropriate safety coverage, escalation paths, operational controls, and alignment with external cloud or enterprise partners.
Identify emerging misuse and severe-harm risks; define ownership and response mechanisms across prevention, detection, investigation, enforcement, and continuous improvement.
Establish meaningful metrics for program delivery, deployment readiness, safety effectiveness, operational quality, and user or developer experience.
Represent customer and developer needs in technical and leadership decisions, balancing risk reduction, model usefulness, implementation complexity, speed, and scale.
Communicate program health, risks, recommendations, and consequential tradeoffs clearly to engineering teams, cross-functional partners, and executives.
Improve delivery and safety outcomes through practical operating mechanisms, scalable tooling, and data- or AI-assisted workflows.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have a strong track record of delivering high-impact technical programs across product, platform, API, infrastructure, machine learning, or safety domains.
Bring strong technical judgment across distributed systems, cloud deployments, public or internal APIs, developer platforms, production machine learning, or scalable product architecture.
Can engage credibly with engineers on system design, implementation tradeoffs, reliability, deployment constraints, and operational risks.
Have delivered platforms or developer-facing capabilities and understand how technical decisions affect customer experience, developer experience, and product usefulness.
Understand how safety, integrity, or abuse-prevention systems work, including evaluations, model guardrails, classifiers, monitoring, enforcement, investigations, and incident response.
Bring strong program management discipline and can coordinate multiple workstreams, resolve complex dependencies, and turn ambiguity into accountable execution.
Demonstrate product judgment and can balance user and customer needs with model usefulness, safety risk, technical complexity, and business priorities.
Communicate clearly and empathetically with engineering teams, executives, policy and legal partners, and external stakeholders.
Are comfortable owning high-stakes programs that require executive presence, cross-organizational influence, and sound decisions under uncertainty.
Have relevant experience with sensitive deployments, major cloud providers, or serious-harm domains such as violent misuse, child safety, cybersecurity, or other emerging threats.
Are hands-on, curious, and motivated to help ensure increasingly capable AI systems are deployed responsibly.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

Job Summary

The Axel Group is currently seeking a Project Manager to join our client’s team in the Orlando, FL area. Our client partners with leading contractors and builders across the commercial, institutional, healthcare, and industrial sectors, providing everything from tools and safety products to custom-fabricated strut grids, pipe hangers, and pre-engineered support systems. With a strong reputation, national footprint, and long-standing relationships throughout the construction industry, the company continues to grow its presence in key markets including healthcare, data centers, infrastructure, and commercial development.

The Project Manager role is a hands-on, high-ownership position focused on managing projects from award through installation and contract closeout. This individual will work closely with general contractors, construction managers, field crews, vendors, customers, and internal leadership to coordinate project requirements, maintain schedules, address issues, and ensure work is completed successfully. The role offers significant autonomy and the opportunity to take ownership of multiple projects while serving as a key point of contact throughout the project lifecycle.

While the position is primarily focused on Project Management, there is also a light estimating and preconstruction component. This includes reviewing drawings and specifications, assisting with material takeoffs, gathering pricing, reviewing project scopes, and supporting estimates and change orders. The ideal candidate does not need to be a career estimator, but should be comfortable reading construction documents, understanding project scope, and working with both field and office teams.

This position offers the opportunity to join a stable, privately held organization with 40+ years of industry experience, a national footprint, and significant resources behind its continued growth. You’ll work on a diverse range of projects while building relationships with some of the industry’s leading contractors and construction professionals. The company provides a competitive compensation package, full benefits including medical, dental, vision, PTO, and 401(k), along with strong opportunities for professional development and long-term career advancement.

Manage multiple construction projects from initial kickoff through installation and final contract closeout.
Take ownership of project execution, ensuring work progresses according to plans, specifications, schedules, budgets, and contractual requirements.
Coordinate project schedules, materials, field installation crews, contractors, vendors, customers, and internal teams.

We’re Fever, the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

As part of the Fever Originals team
, you will leverage data, market insights, and strong commercial instincts to create one-of-a-kind events and experiences that enable people to enjoy unforgettable moments. Our goal is to develop and scale innovative experiences while building strong relationships with venues, partners, and industry stakeholders.

Who You'll Work With

You will join our office in New York City, working closely with internal teams while directly engaging with partners, providers, and venues across the market.

In this role, you will play a key part in growing Fever’s pipeline of original events
. A significant part of your work will involve identifying, developing, and negotiating partnerships with venues and external stakeholders, while collaborating cross-functionally with departments such as Marketing, Operations, and Finance to bring experiences to life.

The team you will join is young, ambitious, and highly collaborative, composed of top profiles from companies such as McKinsey, Amazon, Google, KKR, Cirque du Soleil, PSG, and Roland Garros. Team members bring diverse cultural backgrounds and share a strong entrepreneurial mindset.

Employees are expected to work from the office Monday through Thursday, with the option to work remotely on Fridays.

About the Role:

As a Project Manager, you will work closely with your Regional Lead to develop, launch, and manage Fever Originals experiences from concept to execution. The role combines project management, commercial development, and strategic partnerships, with a strong emphasis on venue negotiations, relationship management, and networking within the local entertainment and events ecosystem.

When you join Fever, you will receive training and coaching to help you:

Identify and develop new business opportunities, including sourcing venues, partners, and collaborators for new event concepts
Lead venue sourcing and contract negotiations, securing optimal terms and building long-term partnerships with strategic venues
Ensure the financial and operational feasibility of our events by analyzing and reporting on key metrics
Drive revenue growth by optimizing ticket sales strategies and identifying opportunities to expand event reach
Analyze business performance, including P&L tracking, forecasting, and operational efficiency improvements
Collaborate cross-functionally with Marketing, Operations, Legal, and Finance teams to ensure successful event launches and smooth operations
Scale successful experiences across additional cities and markets by building replicable operational models
Ensure high-quality experiences, maintaining strong standards for customer satisfaction and operational delivery

About You:

We are looking for someone who combines a strong commercial mindset, relationship-building abilities, and analytical thinking, with a proactive approach to developing partnerships and growing the business.

3+ years of experience in project management, operations, consulting, business development, partnerships, or similar roles (this role is not primarily suited for traditional event planners)
English on a native level, with excellent communication skills
Strong negotiation and networking skills, with the ability to build meaningful partnerships: you’re not afraid of picking up the phone and pitching to potential new partners
Exceptional organizational and project management skills, with the ability to plan, prioritize, and drive multiple workstreams to successful completion.
Resilient and results-driven, able to perform under pressure, take ownership, and manage several high-impact projects in parallel.
Proven ability to build and maintain strong relationships with venues, partners, brands, and stakeholders
Excellent analytical skills, with the ability to use data to guide decision-making
Highly solution-oriented, able to identify challenges and develop practical strategies to resolve them
Ability to work and thrive in fast-paced environments and willingness to grow within the organization

You will join a team of highly effective, motivated, and entrepreneurial professionals who move fast, take ownership, and get things done. Cultural fit means being humble, open to feedback, and willing to learn, while approaching challenges as opportunities and making decisions based on data and insight. We value individuals who are hands-on, collaborative, and able to prioritize what truly drives results. We encourage applicants from diverse and unconventional backgrounds, especially those who bring curiosity, a willingness to learn, and the drive to make a meaningful impact.

Benefits & Perks:

Attractive compensation package and the potential to earn a significant bonus for top performance (Total compensation of 80-98k USD)
Opportunity to have a real impact in a high-growth global category leader
40% discount on all Fever events and experiences
Private health insurance
Gympass Memberships
Work in the heart of the city, with possible travel across our markets
Responsibility from day one and professional and personal growth
Great work environment with a young, international team of talented people to work with!

Our Hiring Process:

A 30 min video call with one of our Talent Acquisition Managers, to better understand your career plan, assess cultural fit and answer any questions you may have
A 60 min online test with three topics: logic, analytics and written understanding
A 45 min video call with your future manager, including questions about your profile and a business case presentation (to be prepared in advance)

On average our process lasts 20 working days and offers usually follow within a week.

The Project Manager will be responsible for managing projects from Notice to Proceed (NTP) and mobilization through construction, commissioning, Substantial Completion and final turnover to the customer/O&M team.

The successful candidate will be accountable for delivering projects safely, on schedule, within budget, in accordance with contract requirements, and to Rethink's quality standards.
The ideal candidate is a hands-on construction project manager who understands how solar projects are actually built and can effectively manage the people, materials, schedule, costs, contracts and issues required to successfully execute a project.

Key Responsibilities

Project Execution & Construction Management

Lead the execution of commercial and industrial rooftop and ground-mount solar projects from NTP through final completion.
Develop and maintain project execution plans and coordinate project mobilization.
Establish clear project objectives, responsibilities, milestones and deliverables for internal teams and subcontractors.
Coordinate engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning activities to ensure successful project execution.
Work closely with the Superintendent, Foremen and field crews to identify and resolve construction issues.
Monitor daily and weekly construction progress and take corrective action when performance does not meet the project plan.
Develop and implement recovery plans when projects fall behind schedule.
Ensure construction activities are performed in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, contract requirements and applicable codes.

Schedule Management

Develop, maintain and actively manage the project baseline schedule.
Establish and manage critical path activities and contractual milestones.
Develop and maintain three-week and other short-term look-ahead schedules as required.
Track project progress against planned production and milestone dates.
Identify schedule risks and develop mitigation and recovery strategies.
Coordinate schedule impacts associated with engineering, permitting, procurement, material deliveries, weather, subcontractors and customer requirements.
Communicate schedule status and potential delays to project leadership and customers in a timely manner.

Subcontractor & Field Team Management

Manage and coordinate subcontractors throughout project execution.
Establish clear expectations for schedule, production, quality, safety, documentation and contract compliance.
Monitor subcontractor performance and address deficiencies promptly.
Review subcontractor schedules, manpower levels and productivity.
Coordinate with field leadership to ensure adequate manpower, equipment and materials are available to maintain the project schedule.
Support subcontractor procurement, scope alignment, negotiations and performance management.

Procurement & Material Management

Coordinate project procurement activities with the estimating, procurement and operations teams.
Track major equipment and material procurement from purchase through delivery to the project site.
Identify long-lead items and material risks that could impact the construction schedule.
Coordinate material deliveries, site logistics and equipment requirements.
Resolve material shortages, damaged materials, incorrect deliveries and other procurement issues that affect project execution.

Cost & Financial Management

Manage project budgets and monitor actual and committed costs against the approved project budget.
Maintain accurate project cost forecasts and identify potential cost exposures.
Review subcontractor invoices, purchase orders and project expenditures.
Identify cost impacts associated with changes, delays, productivity issues and unforeseen conditions.
Work with project leadership to develop and implement cost-control measures.
Support monthly project forecasting and financial reporting.

Contract & Change Management

Manage project execution in accordance with the EPC contract, subcontract agreements, drawings, specifications and other contractual requirements.
Identify changes in scope and document potential cost and schedule impacts.
Prepare and support change order requests, claims and other contractual correspondence.
Ensure required notices are issued in accordance with contractual requirements.
Maintain appropriate documentation to protect Rethink's contractual position.
Monitor subcontractor compliance with contractual obligations.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

Serve as a primary point of contact for the customer during construction.
Lead or participate in weekly construction and project status meetings.
Provide accurate project status updates, including schedule, cost, progress, risks, issues and recovery actions.
Maintain professional relationships with customers, subcontractors, consultants, utilities, AHJs and other project stakeholders.

Quality, Safety & Compliance

Support Rethink's safety culture and ensure project activities are performed in accordance with company safety requirements and project-specific requirements.
Coordinate quality control activities and ensure work complies with approved plans, specifications and applicable codes.

Commissioning, Completion & Turnover

Coordinate construction completion activities with commissioning and operations teams.
Support system energization, testing and commissioning activities.
Manage punch-list development and completion. .

Project Documentation & Reporting

Maintain accurate project records within Procore and other company systems.
Manage RFIs, submittals, meeting minutes, daily reports, schedules, change documentation and other project records.
Prepare weekly and monthly project reports.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Business, Architecture or a related field preferred; equivalent construction experience will be considered.
5+ years of construction project management experience, preferably with commercial/industrial electrical, renewable energy or solar EPC projects.
Demonstrated experience managing construction projects from mobilization through completion and turnover.
Commercial or industrial solar construction experience strongly preferred.
Experience managing subcontractors and field construction teams.
Strong understanding of construction scheduling, project controls, procurement and cost management.
Experience with contract administration, change orders and subcontractor management.
Proficiency with Procore, Microsoft Project, Primavera P6 or similar construction/project management software.
Strong Excel skills and the ability to analyze project cost and schedule information.
Ability to read and understand construction drawings, specifications, contracts and project schedules.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and projects in a fast-paced construction environment.
Willingness to travel to project sites as required.
Strong problem-solving skills with a proactive approach to identifying and resolving project issues.

Location: Vandenberg, CA launch sites or Austin, TX metro area (Relocation Assistance available).

Amentum is seeking an experienced Project Manager
(SME) to support Combatant Command Operations in the Information Environment (OIE) under the Apollo program. The Apollo Solutions Architect Team (ASAT) is a cross-functional enterprise team that drives innovation, standardization, and integration across all Apollo Task Order services. ASAT serves as Apollo’s dedicated SME cell, delivering scalable support to Combatant Commands through advanced solution design, operational integration, training, analysis, and modernization. Centrally based in Tampa, the ASAT continuously develops and deploys new tools, workflows, and TTPs to outpace adversaries and strengthen Combatant Command information advantage.

As a member of ASAT, the selected candidate will manage integrated capability-development projects that improve how Apollo plans, fields, adopts, sustains, and assesses OIE/IW capabilities across Combatant Commands and mission partners. This role applies a holistic capability-lines-of-development approach — including doctrine/TTPs, organization, training, materiel/tools, leadership, personnel, facilities, policy, and process integration — to ensure new capabilities are operationally relevant, adoptable, measurable, scalable, and aligned with Government objectives. The Project Manager (SME) will coordinate cross-functional teams, manage Integrated Project Plans, track risks and dependencies, synchronize stakeholder inputs, and drive implementation of enterprise solutions that improve planning, operations, assessment, mission-enabling services, and decision support.

As a Project Manager (SME), you will:

Manage cross-functional capability-development projects using a holistic lines-of-development approach that considers doctrine/TTPs, organization, training, materiel/tools, leadership, personnel, facilities, policy, processes, data, and sustainment requirements.
Lead development, coordination, execution, and update of Integrated Project Plans (IPPs), including project objectives, milestones, staffing/resource requirements, risks, dependencies, deliverables, implementation schedules, and ROI considerations.
Translate Combatant Command and mission-partner operational needs into executable project plans, implementation roadmaps, decision-support products, and capability-integration strategies.

Develop project management artifacts, including project charters, implementation plans, milestone schedules, risk registers, decision logs, action trackers, project briefs, capability roadmaps, and executive-level status updates.
Identify risks, interdependencies, constraints, and mitigation actions affecting capability implementation, including security, classification, data-access, staffing, stakeholder coordination, technical integration, adoption, training, and sustainment considerations.
Support change management and capability adoption by ensuring users, staffs, planners, analysts, and leadership understand how new tools, workflows, processes, and methodologies improve mission execution.
Coordinate pilot efforts, proof-of-concept activities, capability demonstrations, user-feedback sessions, after-action reviews, and continuous-improvement cycles.
Develop measures of performance, measures of effectiveness, adoption metrics, utilization indicators, and ROI inputs to assess capability value and inform prioritization decisions.
Support integration of advanced technologies, digital tools, data-management approaches, AI-enabled analytics, collaboration platforms, and knowledge-management solutions into operational workflows.

Prepare and deliver executive-level briefings, project status updates, recommendations, decision papers, implementation plans, and lessons-learned products for Government and Amentum leadership.

Sopra Steria biedt op maat gemaakte end-to-end corporate technology en software solutions aan die organisaties helpen gedurfde keuzes te maken en resultaten te boeken. En met succes! The world is how we shape it.

Vacatureomschrijving

Stap in de cruciale wereld van Know Your Customer (KYC) en het bestrijden van financiële criminaliteit (FEC) bij banken en financiële instellingen. Sopra Steria staat aan de frontlinie van het beschermen van het financiële systeem met geavanceerde, data-gedreven Sanction Screening-technologieën. Dit proces detecteert transacties waarbij personen of organisaties betrokken zijn die mogelijk risico’s vormen op het gebied van sancties, terrorismefinanciering of witwassen.

Wat ga je doen?

Als Business Analyst speel je een sleutelrol in het vormgeven, testen en afstemmen van onze sanctie screening systemen en -modellen op het beleid, de risicostandaarden en compliance procedures van de klant. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de volledige levenscyclus van jouw features – van het definiëren van de requirements en begeleiden van de implementatie tot het monitoren van de prestaties en rapporteren van de resultaten. Je bent zowel een strategische denker als een hands-on analist, in staat om complexe zakelijke behoeften te vertalen naar duidelijke en uitvoerbare taken voor jouw squad.

Jouw verantwoordelijkheden/taken zijn:

Specificeren van zakelijke en technische vereisten via interviews, workshops, demo’s en samenwerking
Definiëren van duidelijke en testbare acceptatiecriteria voor features en epics
Prioriteren en onderscheid maken tussen wereldwijde ‘must-haves’ en ‘nice-to-haves’ om de integriteit van wereldwijde standaarden te waarborgen
Analyseren en beoordelen van sanctie screening algoritmen, regels en drempels, en verbeteringen aanbevelen
Nauw samenwerken met Product Owners om backlog refinement en squadprioriteiten af te stemmen
Technische concepten en oplossingen helder communiceren naar internationale stakeholders
Zorgen dat alle oplossingen voldoen aan interne beleidslijnen, standaarden en regelgeving
Uitvoeren van data-analyse en mapping; oplossingen voorstellen voor datakwaliteitsproblemen
Stimuleren van een feedbackcultuur en een proactieve, oplossingsgerichte houding onderhouden

Functie-eisen

Wij zijn op zoek naar gepassioneerde collega’s die graag de grenzen verleggen op het gebied van digitale transformatie en technologieconsultancy. Bij Sopra Steria krijg je de kans om je vaardigheden verder te ontwikkelen in een constructieve, samenwerkende teamomgeving, waarbij je werkt aan impactvolle projecten die verandering teweegbrengen voor onze klanten. Als je gedijt op uitdagingen en (de meeste van) de onderstaande kwalificaties bezit, kijken we uit naar je sollicitatie!

Type dienstverband: Hybride

Locatie: Nieuwegein

Aantal uren: 32-40 uur werkweek

Contractduur: Eén jaar, met uitzicht op een vast dienstverband

Opleiding: Je hebt een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding afgerond

Talen: Nederlands (vereist)

We zoeken iemand met de volgende vaardigheden:

Minimaal 2,5 jaar relevante werkervaring als business analyst, bij voorkeur in de financiële sector
Ervaring met Sanction Screening of bredere FEC-domeinen is zeer gewenst (maar geen must)
Bekendheid met risico- en compliance-architectuur, inclusief tools zoals Inform RiskShield, Python, Databricks
Affiniteit met data analyse: in staat om data lineage analyses, kwaliteitsbeoordelingen en privacy reviews uit te voeren
Ervaring met modeltesten, risicostandaarden en rapportages aan toezichthouders
Vaardigheid om samen te werken met diverse stakeholders zoals Compliance, IT en Business Operations
Sterk functioneel inzicht in enterprise IT-landschappen
Ervaring met Agile, Scrum, DevOps, Lean of SAFe methodologieën

Daarnaast breng je de volgende persoonlijke vaardigheden mee:

Sterk analytisch denkvermogen en probleemoplossend vermogen
In staat om zowel strategisch als gedetailleerd te werken
Uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden, met het vermogen om technische en niet-technische stakeholders te betrekken
Hoog niveau van documentatie- en rapportagevaardigheden – nauwkeurig, onderbouwd en audit-ready
Zelfstandig en georganiseerd, met het vermogen om meerdere initiatieven tegelijk te managen

Aanvullende informatie

Je zal deel uitmaken van een grote naam in de tech wereld die bekend is om consulting, digitale diensten en softwareontwikkeling. Je begeeft je tussen high-level professionals die durven in te zetten om hoge resultaten te behalen. Daarnaast maak je ook deel uit van onze Data area.

Bij Sopra Steria – Financial Economic Crime (FEC) voorzien we banken en financiële instellingen van digitale tools om risico’s te beheren, klanten te beschermen en de impact van financiële economische criminaliteit te beperken. Als poortwachters van het financiële systeem spelen banken een cruciale rol in de bescherming van onze economie tegen criminele inmenging. Daardoor worden financiële instellingen onderworpen aan steeds strengere regelgeving en toezicht. Tegelijkertijd maken wereldwijde economische instabiliteit en steeds geavanceerdere, technologiegedreven financiële criminaliteit het werk van banken steeds moeilijker.

Enkele cijfers: Naar schatting wordt jaarlijks 16 miljard euro aan crimineel geld witgewassen in Nederland. Minder dan 1% van de criminele geldstromen die via het mondiale banksysteem gaan, wordt daadwerkelijk gestopt. Daarom moeten banken hun aanpak radicaal veranderen in de strijd tegen FEC. Gelukkig zijn er tactische veranderingen die banken snel kunnen doorvoeren om het effect van financiële economische criminaliteit te verminderen.

Bij Sopra Steria zorgen we ervoor dat jij je werk met plezier én in balans kunt doen. Daarom bieden we een aantrekkelijk en flexibel pakket aan arbeidsvoorwaarden:

Sociale activiteiten met collega’s, van gezellige borrels tot sportieve of inhoudelijke uitjes;
Ontwikkelmogelijkheden via trainingen, kennisdelingssessies en inspirerende (netwerk)events;
Hybride werken: thuis of op kantoor, afhankelijk van wat jij nodig hebt;
Een royaal mobiliteitsbudget, in de vorm van een leaseregeling van €892,- met de keuze uit een elektrische leaseauto met NS Business Card of leasefiets of een alternatief vervoersregeling van €1.007,- net wat het beste bij jouw manier van reizen past;
Winstdeling van 8% on target;
27 betaalde vakantiedagen
Mogelijkheid om op fiscaal vriendelijke manier studieschuld af te lossen, een fiets, zonnepanelen of sportabonnementen aan te schaffen (Cafetaria-systeem) of andere personeelskortingen te verkrijgen;
Een internetvergoeding en thuiswerkvergoeding waarbij wij jou faciliteiten bieden voor de uitrusting van jouw eigen thuiskantoor;
Een flexibele pensioenregeling, waaraan jij, op maat en passend bij jou, bijdragen kunt toevoegen.

jobs.description:
Company Overview

The Center for International Private Enterprise (CIPE) strengthens democracy around the world through private enterprise and market-oriented reform. CIPE is one of the four core institutes of the National Endowment for Democracy and is an affiliate of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. Since 1983, CIPE has worked with business leaders, policymakers, and civil society to build the institutions vital to a democratic society. CIPE’s key program areas include Enterprise Ecosystems, Democratic Governance, Business Advocacy, Women’s Economic Empowerment, Anti-Corruption & Ethics, and Trade.

Position:
Senior Program Manager
Reports to:
Regional Hub Director, Europe and Eurasia
Period of Performance:
September 2026 – March 31st 2027

Scope:
CIPE is seeking a full-time, exempt position based in Washington, D.C. for a Senior Program Manager for Central Asia. This position is responsible for the development and implementation of CIPE’s strategic focus on democratic governance through private sector collective action initiatives to improve business participation, economic freedom, and opportunity across the region by developing regional and country strategies, communications strategies, project implementation, and support grants to local business organizations, think tanks, and chambers of commerce. The position will manage CIPE’s U.S. Department of State-funded Central Asia Migration Entrepreneurship Program (CAMEP) and UK FCDO-funded “Equipping Central Asian Business to Navigate Global Economic Security Issues – Phase II” project.

Responsibilities:

Contribute to the development and implementation of strategy for accomplishing CIPE’s objectives on improving democratic governance and advancing market reforms in region.
Design, implement, and manage a portfolio of projects and grants for the assigned region, supportive of CIPE’s overall goals and strategies for target countries. Project responsibilities have the following dimensions:
Develop project concept papers, proposals, reports, and correspondence.
Act as CIPE’s representative to promote democratic market-oriented institutional reforms in region including developing and implementing training programs, public speaking at events, and facilitating meetings with partners, potential partners, and other stakeholders.
Lead and contribute to business development efforts by drafting full proposals narratives, technical sections of proposal narratives, budget inputs, or other thematic documents.
Analyze, research, and be familiar with the region’s political and economic landscape, identifying opportunities for CIPE programs and partners.
Identify potential partner organizations and beneficiaries in country and collaborate to design effective democratic and economic-reform programs.
Analyze both solicited and unsolicited project proposals in the context of the regional socio-political context, CIPE strategy, grant guidelines, and criteria.
Collaborate with partners to refine project proposals, monitoring and evaluation plans, and project budgets.
Implement, monitor, and manage all project activities, in collaboration with local partner organizations and CIPE team members.
Establish and maintain regular communication with project partners and other stakeholders.
Maintain correspondence and operational records regarding CIPE-funded programs in the assigned portfolio.
Monitor grantees, contractors, and consultants’ performance to ensure full compliance with objectives, financial and reporting requirements, and evaluation plans.
Evaluate projects through on-site visits, file reviews, and coordination with independent evaluators where appropriate.
Develop project reports, summaries, and assessments.
Provide oversight of CIPE country representatives across the assigned portfolio, includes supervision and leadership on all project activities, budgets, and expenditures.
Responsible for the financial management and stewardship of funds, including monitoring project spending, projecting future expenses, approving expenditures, and developing accurate budget for new projects. May include financial and operational management of a field office.
Establish and maintain relationships with other donor organizations to identify linkages with CIPE strategies, monitor trends, and assess new funding opportunities. Work with the U.S. State Department, UK FCDO, and other assistance programs to develop joint projects, grants and/or contracts to further democratic and economic reform initiatives.
Establish technical expertise, translating program experiences into lessons learned for internal and external stakeholders. Facilitate staff building technical expertise in thematic areas of work through leading staff training, developing internal resources, and/or leading staff working groups.
Collaborate with multiple CIPE departments to achieve programmatic goals, including Communications, Grants and Finance, Policy and Program Learning, and other regional teams.
Monitor current events, including political and economic changes, and US relations in region and assess the impact on ongoing and planned CIPE projects.
Adhere to appropriate CIPE, National Endowment for Democracy (NED), and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce policies and procedures.
Significant management responsibilities, including:
Supervise, develop and manage program staff, including Program Associates, Program Coordinators, field staff and consultants, when applicable.
Assist Director with planning for team growth, recruitment, and performance monitoring.
Contribute extensively to external communications include authoring blogs for CIPE’s website, op-eds for external publications, participating in podcasts, and participating in major public-speaking engagements on a quarterly basis.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in one of the following fields is required: International Relations, International Business, Economic Development, Political Science, Regional/Area Studies or Public Policy.
Master’s degree, or the equivalent experience in International Relations, International Business, Economic Development, Political Science, or Public Policy is preferred.
7+ years of experience in international assistance programs, non-profit organizations, chambers of commerce, and/or associations in region, preferably in the assigned countries.
Minimum five years’ experience with program management and program implementation at the strategic level, preferred.
Experience with international development and topics consistent with CIPE’s mission, including anti-corruption and business ethics, democratic governance, business association advocacy, entrepreneurship and others.
Prior experience with UK FCDO-funded programs is preferred.
Prior experience with U.S. Department of State-funded programs is preferred.
Demonstrated project management in NGOs.
Demonstrated ability to develop, establish, and maintain good relationships with international partners, donors, and colleagues.
Fluency (written and spoken) in [language] required; knowledge of [additional] languages preferred.
Strong public speaking and writing skills with attention to detail.
Proposal writing skills is required.
Demonstrated strong critical thinking and analytical skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced, team environment, as well as independently with minimum supervision; ability to prioritize and handle multiple tasks.
Ability to supervise, develop and manage young professionals and other staff, when applicable.
Proficiency in MS-Office, specifically Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Must be able and willing to travel for extended and multiple periods.
High degree of culture competence.
Contribute to an organization-wide culture of innovation, integrity, inclusion, and respect.
Strong conceptual, verbal, and written communication skills.
Ability to take initiative, organize tasks, and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced, time-sensitive environment, ensuring deadlines are met with attention to detail.
Skilled in building strong, trusting relationships to gain support and achieve desired outcomes.
Capable of managing multiple competing priorities simultaneously.
Comfortable working in an environment with international objectives.
Flexible and able to engage with individuals at all levels with strong interpersonal skills
Proficiency with MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook required.

Benefits and Perks

Role Description

SMBC is seeking a highly analytical Analyst to support reporting, metrics, and business intelligence activities within Anti-Fraud Operations Governance Team. This role will be responsible for producing and analyzing fraud management reports, operational dashboards, key risk indicators (KRIs), and executive-level metrics used to monitor fraud trends, operational performance, and fraud losses.

Produce and distribute daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly fraud operations reports and dashboards.

Develop executive-level reporting packages for senior management, committees, audits, and regulatory examinations.
Monitor reporting accuracy and perform data quality reviews to ensure integrity and consistency of management information.
Identify trends, anomalies, and emerging fraud risks through data analysis and reporting.
Create and maintain dashboards, scorecards, and visualizations using reporting and analytics tools.
Support recurring reporting for governance forums, risk committees, and leadership meetings.
Partner with Technology and data teams to automate reporting processes and improve reporting efficiency.
Assist with regulatory exams, audits, and information requests by gathering, validating, and presenting data.
Track operational performance against established service level agreements (SLAs), KPIs, and departmental objectives.
Maintain reporting procedures, methodologies, and documentation.
Support ad hoc analysis and special projects related to fraud trends, operational effectiveness, and strategic initiatives.

1-3 years of experience in reporting, analytics, operations, risk management, fraud operations, or financial services.
Strong analytical and quantitative skills with the ability to interpret large data sets.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including Pivot Tables, formulas, and data analysis functions.
Experience creating reports, dashboards, and management presentations.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Managed Services
jobs.description:
**Description**


At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ mission success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainable practices. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business. Our workforce enjoys career enrichment opportunities available through mobility and development, while experiencing rewarding relationships with supportive supervisors and talented colleagues and customers. Your most important work is ahead.


If this sounds like the kind of environment where you can thrive, then keep reading because Leidos is seeking a qualified **Program Manager** to join our team. The successful candidate will be a customer\-focused Senior IT Program leader who thrives on complex, high\-visibility federal transformation efforts.

* This position is onsite /hybrid. Candidates must reside within the DMV area, preferably near **Bethesda, MD,** and **Gaithersburg MD**.

**Key Responsibilities:**


The Program Manager will own full contract performance across 10 integrated task areas spanning data center operations, network services, compute/storage/cloud (AWS, Azure, and GCP), enterprise services, laboratory IT support, cross\-functional services, client advocacy, program/project management, and transition services.

**Additional Duties:**

* Serve as the single point of accountability for overall program performance — scope, schedule, cost/budget, quality, staffing, and risk — across all 10 Task Areas of the contract.
* Own and maintain the Program Management Plan (PMP), Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), Risk Management Plan, Subcontractor Management Plan, Communications Plan, Staffing Plan, and Quality Assurance Plan (QAP).
* Lead the three\-phase transition (Transition Planning, Transition, and Cutover to Managed Services), in coordination with the Transition Manager, including oversight of the GFP equipment buyout and the Ashburn data center lease takeover from the incumbent contractor.
* Represent Leidos at the Strategic Layer (Executive Committee) of the joint FDA/Contractor governance structure; support Tactical Layer (Steering Committee) and Operational Layer (weekly service delivery) governance as needed.
* Identify, align, and manage qualified resources across all contract task areas; maintain the contractor organizational chart and full personnel roster for FDA visibility.
* Direct and mentor a senior leadership team including the Deputy Program Manager, Transition Manager, Task Area Leads (Data Center Operations, Network Services, Cloud \& Compute/Storage, Enterprise Services, Lab Support, Cross\-Functional Services), Client Advocate/Technical Leads, Service Delivery Manager, Program Security Officer/ISSM, and Financial/Chargeback Manager.
* Drive the multi\-cloud migration strategy (AWS, Azure, GCP landing zones) covering roughly 60% of FDA applications, while ensuring continued high\-quality operation of the \~40% of workloads remaining in the Contractor\-Owned, Contractor\-Operated (COCO) data center environment.
* Establish and operate a simplified, transparent cloud/data\-center chargeback ("pass\-thru") model that FDA's individual Centers can readily understand and administer.
* Ensure staffing and skill levels remain adequate to meet FDA's service objectives; coordinate all contractor onboarding/offboarding and required training/certification compliance (e.g., FDA Records Management Training, Computer Security Awareness Training, IT Security Recertification).
* Own monthly and ad hoc reporting to the COR, including the Monthly Financial Report (MFR), performance\-metric reporting against Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and responses to Government data calls, audits, and security assessments.
* Manage subcontractor and vendor relationships (including hyperscale cloud providers and legacy ITSM tool vendors) to ensure integrated, seamless service delivery.
* Proactively manage program risk, including the financial and operational risk inherent in transitioning from a T\&M/GOCO structure to an FFP/COCO structure, aging on\-premises infrastructure (White Oak), accrued technology debt, and reliance on third\-party cloud providers.
* Lead Transition\-Out planning and execution at contract end (or upon re\-compete loss), ensuring an orderly, low\-risk handover of services, assets, and documentation.
* Ensure compliance with FDA policies, procedures, and standards (including NARA records schedules and FDA Staff Manual Guides) and with all applicable federal acquisition and IT governance requirements.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree and 12\+ years of progressive experience managing large\-scale federal IT infrastructure, data center, or managed\-services contracts or a master’s degree with 10\+ years of prior relevant experience. Additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
* 7\+ years in a Program Manager or equivalent senior leadership role on a program of comparable scope and value.
* Demonstrated success managing both Firm\-Fixed\-Price (FFP) and Time \& Materials (T\&M) contract types, ideally including a T\&M\-to\-FFP or GOCO\-to\-COCO (or similar ownership\-model) transition.
* Proven experience overseeing large\-scale IT transition/transformation efforts, including asset transfer, facility/lease takeover, or similar high\-stakes transition activities.
* Strong working knowledge of hybrid/multi\-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, and/or Google Cloud Platform) and of enterprise data center operations.
* Experience establishing and operating IT service governance structures (e.g., Executive/Steering/Operational committee models) with a federal civilian customer.
* Excellent executive communication, negotiation, and relationship\-management skills, with demonstrated ability to serve as the primary customer\-facing interface for a Contracting Officer, COR, and senior agency stakeholders.
* U.S. Citizenship.
* M

* Communication \& Collaboration: Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate with stakeholders at all levels.
* Problem\-solving and Critical Thinking: Strong analytical and critical thinking skills to identify challenges, evaluate alternatives, and recommend effective solutions.
* Excellent communication, interpersonal, and collaboration skills, with the ability to build rapport, resolve conflicts, and drive consensus among stakeholders.
* Analytical mindset with the ability to assess complex situations, identify root causes, and develop pragmatic solutions to address them.
* Proficiency in Agile tools and techniques for project management, collaboration, and tracking (e.g., JIRA, Confluence) is desirable.

Our data center solutions are tailored to our customers’ needs and delivered by our exceptional end-to-end team. Ready to join us in transforming the future of data centers and sustainability? Apply now to explore exciting career opportunities at Rowan Digital Infrastructure and be a part of our mission to revolutionize data center delivery.

Role Summary

Rowan Digital Infrastructure is looking for a Project Manager – Onsite Power Delivery to lead the end-to-end planning, coordination, and delivery of on-site behind-the-meter (BTM) power infrastructure supporting large-scale data center developments across Rowan Digital Infrastructure’s growing portfolio.

This role oversees the delivery of the onsite microgrid power plants that support our data center campuses using combinations of gas fired turbines, reciprocal generators, BESS solutions, as well as the related electrical infrastructure from early design through commissioning and energization.

The Project Manager (PM) – Onsite Power Delivery role serves as the primary point of integration between our hyperscale customers, Rowan’s commercial and energy teams, as well as our engineering, equipment, construction contractors, commissioning partners and ultimately Rowan operations. The PM will ensure power infrastructure is delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in alignment with long-term operational requirements. This role proactively manages technical risk, long-lead equipment strategy, permitting, and interconnection milestones to protect overall project delivery.

Travel: Ability to travel up to 50% for company gatherings and to project sites

Compensation: 150k-180K (Plus bonus)

Location: Can be based at site location or remote

Essential Responsibilities

Project Leadership & Execution

Lead planning and execution of all power infrastructure scopes including:
Onsite Microgrid delivery
Substations (AIS/GIS)
Medium- and high-voltage distribution
Switchgear and protection systems
Develop and manage project schedules aligned with overall campus milestones
Ensure coordination between power engineering, civil, structural, and MEP scopes impacting power delivery
Drive early risk identification and mitigation planning

Utility & Stakeholder Management

Coordinate with AHJs and permitting authorities
Partner with internal development, procurement, finance, and operations teams to align infrastructure delivery with customer capacity commitments

Cost & Contract Management

Develop and manage power delivery infrastructure budgets
Oversee bid packages, contractor selection, and contract negotiations
Track and manage change orders specific to electrical and utility scopes
Monitor long-lead equipment procurement (transformers, switchgear, breakers, generators)
Forecast cost risk tied to material pricing and supply chain constraints

Technical Oversight

Review design documents for constructability, phasing strategy, and operational resilience
Validate redundancy, resiliency, and scalability requirements
Ensure protection studies, arc flash analysis, and commissioning plans are incorporated
Coordinate factory witness testing and on-site commissioning activities
Schedule & Risk Management
Develop detailed energization milestone plans

Identify Schedule Risk Tied To

Power engineering and delivery
Equipment manufacturing
Mitigation planning for long-lead items and grid constraints
Provide clear reporting on power readiness status to executive leadership

Safety & Compliance

Ensure adherence to high-voltage safety protocols
Oversee compliance with utility standards and electrical codes
Support development of energization procedures and turnover documentation

Reporting & Executive Communication

Provide concise, data-driven updates on:
Power capacity milestones
Cost exposure
Delivery risk
Long-lead equipment tracking
Elevate issues early with recommended solutions

Education, Skills, And Experience

5–10+ years of experience managing large-scale infrastructure or electrical construction projects including significant experience with the engineering, procurement and construction delivery of onsite, behind-the-meter microgrid power solutions, including the use of natural gas and renewables
Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related technical field
Professional certifications such as PMP (Project Management Professional) or PE (Professional Engineer) preferred but not required
Additional training or certifications related to high-voltage systems or power systems considered a plus
Experience delivering medium- and high-voltage electrical systems, substations, or utility interconnections
Experience working on data centers, mission-critical facilities, energy infrastructure, or large industrial projects preferred
Demonstrated experience managing contractors, consultants, and utility providers.
Experience managing project budgets, schedules, procurement, and change orders.
Experience coordinating long-lead electrical equipment procurement (transformers, switchgear, generators)
Familiarity with commissioning and energization processes for electrical infrastructure

Fueled by Excellence & Collaboration

At Rowan, we are a distributed team united by a common mission to transform data center delivery. Across our two offices, we offer a hybrid work environment supported by teamwork, technology, and in-office gathering time to help you be successful. We are headquartered in downtown Denver, Colorado and have an office in Seattle, Washington. Our team of talented and passionate individuals is spread out across the U.S.

At Rowan, we want to make sure you can do great work. We offer competitive benefits focused on helping you be and achieve your best.

Hybrid working environment
Team building and educational opportunities
Generous benefits package including robust health benefits and a 401(k)-company contribution
Unlimited PTO
RTD ECO pass or parking reimbursement
Competitive compensation, bonus, and an incentive plan
