jobs.description:
Job Summary

Project Manager - Critical Operations IT System Modernization

We are seeking an experienced Contractor Project Manager to lead a high-priority Operations IT initiative focused on developing a new system with the support of AI-assisted development practices to help accelerate, support, and improve aspects of the development process. The effort will support modernization of a current legacy system written in Ingres and OpenROAD and will require close coordination across multiple business, technology, operations, security, data, and vendor teams. This role is ideal for a delivery-focused project manager who can bring structure, urgency, and clear communication to a complex, highly visible project with operational impact.

Key Responsibilities

Lead end-to-end project planning, execution, tracking, and delivery for a critical Operations IT project focused on developing a new system to replace or modernize the legacy environment.
Develop and maintain project plans, timelines, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, and status reporting.
Coordinate activities across multiple internal teams, including Operations, IT, application development, data, cybersecurity, infrastructure, change management, compliance, and business stakeholders.
Facilitate working sessions, project meetings, decision reviews, and executive-level updates.
Drive accountability across project contributors and ensure deliverables are completed on time and aligned with scope.
Partner with technical leads and subject matter experts to translate business needs into actionable project tasks and delivery plans.
Coordinate legacy system discovery and modernization planning related to the existing Ingres and OpenROAD environment, including dependencies, integration points, business rules, risks, and transition needs.
Support planning for the responsible use of AI-assisted tools and practices during the development process, including coordination around standards, governance, testing, validation, documentation, and delivery controls.
Identify project risks early, escalate blockers appropriately, and recommend practical mitigation strategies.
Ensure smooth handoffs, documentation, implementation readiness, and post-deployment support planning.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of project management experience leading complex IT, operations technology, application delivery, or enterprise transformation projects.
Demonstrated experience managing cross-functional teams and coordinating work across business and technical stakeholders.
Strong understanding of project management practices, including scope management, schedule management, risk management, issue tracking, dependency management, and stakeholder communications.
Experience delivering projects in fast-paced, mission-critical, or operationally sensitive environments.
Ability to communicate clearly with technical teams, business leaders, executives, vendors, and end users.
Strong meeting facilitation, documentation, follow-up, and decision-tracking skills.
Comfort working on projects where AI-assisted tools, automation, analytics, data-driven practices, or emerging technologies may be used to support delivery.
Proficiency with project management and collaboration tools such as Microsoft Project, Azure DevOps, Jira, Smartsheet, Planner, Teams, SharePoint, or similar platforms.

Preferred Experience

Experience with projects that use AI-assisted development, automation, analytics, data integration, or modern software delivery practices to support implementation.
Experience managing legacy application modernization, replacement, migration, or re-platforming initiatives, especially involving older database or application development environments such as Ingres, OpenROAD, or similar technologies.
Experience working in operations, utility, energy, critical infrastructure, regulated, or high-availability environments.
PMP, PMI-ACP, Scrum Master, SAFe, or similar project/program management certification.
Experience managing vendor resources, system integrators, consultants, or third-party technology partners.
Familiarity with change management, training coordination, user adoption, operational readiness, and production support transition planning.

Engagement Details

Role Type: Contractor
Project Area: Operations IT, legacy system modernization, AI-assisted development support, and cross-functional delivery
Work Style: Collaborative, hands-on, delivery-oriented, and highly communicative
Primary Focus: Keeping a critical project organized, visible, actionable, and moving forward across multiple teams

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a proactive, detail-oriented project manager who can quickly understand business priorities, organize complex workstreams, and build alignment across diverse teams. They should be comfortable operating in ambiguity, asking the right questions, escalating risks early, and maintaining momentum on a critical initiative where communication, accountability, and delivery discipline are essential.

Traveling opportunities
Great work environment

The GSD Program Management Office (PMO) is responsible for organizational alignment with the GSD growth goal and approach. Through leveraging a deep appreciation of the objectives and needs of GSD’s most demanding customers and highest risk initiatives, the PMO is uniquely positioned to create and deploy effective frameworks, systems, and program managers to defend GSD’s Big Bet strategy so that GSD can fullfill its Strategic Growth Intent.

Position Summary

GSD PMO Program Managers drive multi-site GSD strategic initiatives and ensure alignment with organization goals. This role oversees one or more initiatives, including establishing governance frameworks, managing risks, and monitoring performance. For initiatives under their purview, the Program Manager engages with customers and stakeholders at all levels as an initiative champion to enhance project delivery and organizational efficiency.

Program Managers also support the definition of and execution against annual PMO plans and roadmaps, as well as contribute to the annual strategic intent process. With a strong background in stakeholder management and leadership, PMO Program Managers will play a critical role in achieving business success and fostering a culture of excellence.

This is not a project management or site-specific position. This is a strategic role across GSD sites, projects, and teams to align individual and site team results with GSD goals and customer needs.

This is an exciting position where individuals with passion for solving problems, collaborating with teams, and creating repeatable success thrive.

Duties And Responsibilities

Program management and oversight of one or more multi-site GSD Strategic Initiatives, including but not limited to:
Understands internal and external stakeholder needs and expectations
Identifies roadblocks to success, and establishes effective actions to overcome
Establishes, educates and enforces governance frameworks and success criteria,
Proactively identifies, assesses, and mitigates project risks and issues, ensuring timely resolution and minimal impact on project delivery.
Monitors performance against program metrics, providing actionable insights and recommendations to stakeholders.
Ensures adherence to best practices, standards, and regulatory requirements.
Fosters strong relationships with customers, project teams, stakeholders, and executive management, ensuring effective communication and collaboration.
Creates, uses, and deploys programmatic frameworks, tools, and systems.
Provides program level leadership including oversight, guidance, and functional management.
Works with commercial and site teams to drive growth and meet new market needs aligned with GSD Strategy, including new product development, technology deployment, and ensuring scalability.
Identifies growth opportunities within customers and markets by bringing holistic capability view.
Contributes to the creation of PMO goals, plans, and roadmaps, as well as the execution against the resulting Office priority projects.
Contributes to the annual GSD Strategic Intent process, including formulation and revision of Strategic Initiatives. Provides key inputs to define technology roadmaps, commercial initiatives, and customer insights.
Champions GSD Strategy and Initiatives to the sites.
Serves as a trusted advocate representing both key customers to the sites as well as the sites to key customers.
Creates, effectively writes, and communicates multi-site proposals to customers.
May support the onboarding and development of new GSD program managers.
May serve as an interim primary point of contact for customers until an account manager is determined.
Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong customer orientation.
Superior communication and interpersonal skills.
Strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities.
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple complex projects simultaneously.
Able to lead, prioritize and oversee multiple large-scale efforts in a fast-paced environment with proven ability to meet deadlines.
Superior attention to detail, organization, and planning skills.
Able to manage changing priorities and ambiguity while remaining focused.
Advanced proficiency in project management software and tools.
Ability to acquire substantial knowledge of sites’ manufacturing processes, procedures and products.
Ability to travel as needed to meet with customers, team members or company events.

Characteristics

Uncompromising integrity
Solutions oriented
Committed to personal development; seeks feedback and challenges self.
Leadership and Collaboration: Provides exceptional leadership, guiding project teams and promoting a collaborative work environment.
Results-Oriented: Ability to set and meet ambitious goals and performance targets.
Adaptability: Ability to pivot strategies as needed to stay competitive.
Consistently models Global Space and Defense Team Behaviors to customers and site teams.
Low Ego. Lives the IDEX Values of Trust, Team, and Excellence.

Credentials And Experience

Bachelor's degree or higher in a relevant engineering or science field or in Business Administration. Advanced degrees in engineering or technical fields preferred.
Technical experience in R&D, production, and engineering environments.
Experience driving organizational change and process improvement.
Experience managing multi-person and/or multifunctional projects.

The Project Manager
is responsible for leading the end-to-end planning, execution, integration, and delivery of ICT infrastructure, network, systems, and cybersecurity projects within complex multi-vendor, multi-platform environments. The role requires effective coordination of internal cross-functional teams, external vendors, and customer stakeholders to ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with agreed scope and quality standards.

The successful candidate will possess strong project governance capabilities, stakeholder management experience, technical acumen, and the ability to navigate complex delivery environments while maintaining a high level of customer satisfaction.

Key Responsibilities

Project Planning & Delivery:
Lead and manage the full project lifecycle from initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closure.
Develop and maintain detailed project plans, schedules, resource allocations, risk registers, and delivery milestones.
Ensure successful delivery of infrastructure, network, systems, and integrated technology solutions within agreed scope, budget, quality, and timeline.
Coordinate project activities across internal teams, external partners, subcontractors, and vendors.
Monitor project progress proactively and implement corrective actions where required to maintain project objectives.

Resource & Vendor Management:
Manage internal project resources and external vendors to ensure delivery commitments and project milestones are achieved.
Resolve resource allocation conflicts across multiple concurrent projects and business priorities.
Establish and maintain effective vendor governance mechanisms, ensuring supplier performance meets contractual and operational requirements.
Oversee procurement activities and ensure the accuracy, timeliness, and completeness of project-related procurement and material delivery.

Stakeholder & Customer Management:
Serve as the primary point of contact for customers throughout the project lifecycle.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with customer stakeholders, fostering trust and long-term partnerships.
Establish and maintain a consistent engagement cadence with customers through project reviews, governance meetings, and progress updates.
Conduct project kick-off meetings, project status reviews, steering committee meetings, and customer presentations.
Manage customer expectations and negotiate project-related issues, discrepancies, scope changes, and delivery challenges professionally and effectively.

Project Governance & Risk Management:
Identify, assess, monitor, and mitigate project risks and issues throughout project execution.
Manage project scope changes and variations through established change management processes.
Handle project escalations promptly and drive issues to closure with appropriate stakeholder engagement.
Ensure incidents occurring during project implementation are managed, documented, escalated, and resolved in accordance with company processes.
Drive adherence to project governance standards, delivery methodologies, and quality assurance practices.

Documentation & Reporting:
Prepare and deliver accurate, timely, and comprehensive project reports for internal and customer stakeholders.
Ensure all project documentation, reports, deliverables, and technical records comply with company standards and quality requirements.
Maintain proper project records for governance, audit, operational handover, and project closure purposes.

Business Development Support:
Support the Sales and Pre-Sales teams during bid, tender, and proposal phases.
Participate in project sizing, solution reviews, risk assessments, effort estimation, and project planning activities.
Contribute project management expertise to improve proposal quality, delivery feasibility, and commercial competitiveness.

Qualifications & Certifications

Valid Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or Certified IT Project Manager (CITPM) certification.

Skills & Experience

Experience:
Minimum 5 years of project management experience delivering ICT infrastructure, networking, systems integration, or technology transformation projects.
Proven track record managing medium to large-scale projects involving multiple stakeholders, vendors, and cross-functional teams.

Technical Competencies:
Strong understanding of enterprise infrastructure, networking, systems, cloud platforms, and integrated technology environments.
Ability to comprehend technical solution designs and assess implementation risks.
Engineering background with knowledge of structured cabling and patching infrastructure is advantageous.

Professional Skills:
Strong project planning, scheduling, tracking, monitoring, reporting, and project closure capabilities.
Expertise in vendor and supplier management, including contract and performance management.
Strong stakeholder and customer relationship management skills.
Excellent conflict resolution and negotiation skills, particularly in managing project constraints, resource challenges, and customer expectations.
Ability to assess project complexity, identify risks early, and develop effective mitigation strategies.
Strong communication and presentation skills, with experience engaging stakeholders at both technical and management levels.
Resilient, customer-focused, and able to perform effectively under pressure in dynamic project environments.
Demonstrated ability to drive accountability and achieve successful project outcomes in challenging delivery scenarios.

Success Measures

The Project Manager will be measured on:

On-time project delivery.
Budget adherence and financial performance.
Customer satisfaction and relationship management.
Quality of project deliverables and documentation.
Effective risk, issue, and escalation management.
Successful coordination of internal teams and external vendors.

Escalate Effectively: Analyze findings to determine the scope and severity of incidents, resolving straightforward issues and escalating complex cases to Level 2 Analysts with clear, concise information.
Security Tool Management: Review and implement authorized, routine changes to security tools, such as processing client exemption requests in the EDR or temporarily adjusting settings for testing.
Collaborate with the Security Team: Work closely with fellow analysts and security engineers, sharing information, participating in team discussions, and contributing to a collaborative security environment.

Provide Support: Offer timely and helpful support related to security inquiries, upholding a professional and customer-service-oriented approach in all interactions.

Security + Certification

Job Description

Staff Program Intelligence Analyst

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard – from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.

The Role

We’re seeking a strategic, hands-on Staff-level individual contributor to set direction and deliver the future of Program Intelligence, analytics, and AI across the Program Management organization. This role operates at the intersection of enterprise data strategy, storytelling, and portfolio execution — enabling senior leadership to make faster, smarter decisions through trusted, high-quality, actionable insights. The successful candidate will work with broad autonomy, navigate significant ambiguity, and influence outcomes across organizational boundaries without direct authority.

You will define and advance the Program Intelligence strategy, establishing scalable patterns, standards, and governance for data products (dashboards, AI Agents, web applications, and analytics pipelines). You’ll work directly with PMO leaders and cross-functional partners to deliver high-impact, customer-facing capabilities and narratives that connect data to business outcomes. You will also raise the capability of the broader organization through mentoring, coaching, and reusable practices while remaining an individual contributor.

Why This Role Matters

GM’s vehicle portfolio is evolving faster than ever and demands sharper insight and tighter alignment across the enterprise. This role defines how Program Management measures what matters — turning data into the connective tissue between strategy, capacity, and execution. The impact of this role extends beyond individual deliverables: it establishes the intelligence capabilities, decision frameworks, and operating standards that enable leaders and teams to execute with greater clarity and speed.

What You’ll Do

Set the Program Intelligence & Reporting Strategy: Define and evolve the long-term vision, principles, operating model, and architecture for management information, reporting, analytics, and dashboards that support portfolio, capacity, and delivery decision-making.
Lead portfolio-scale data products: Direct the design and delivery of trusted, decision-grade dashboards, AI Agents, web applications, and reports that establish a durable source of truth for program health, capacity, and delivery performance.
Establish metrics and data governance: Create common definitions, measurement frameworks, data quality expectations, and governance practices that improve consistency, comparability, and confidence in enterprise decisions.
Architect analytics and AI solutions: Translate ambiguous, high-impact business needs into scalable data models, analytical products, AI-driven solutions, and reusable technical patterns in partnership with data engineering, IT, and product teams.
Influence executive decisions: Synthesize complex data and competing perspectives into clear narratives, recommendations, and decision frameworks that drive alignment and action at the senior leadership level.
Drive adoption and measurable value: Champion the use of Program Intelligence capabilities, assess adoption and business impact, and continuously improve products and practices based on customer feedback and evolving portfolio needs.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Data Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
5+ years of progressive experience in business intelligence, analytics, data products, management reporting, or a related discipline, including experience leading complex, enterprise-level initiatives.
Advanced experience with SQL, Python, cloud analytics platforms (e.g., Databricks, AWS), and the development or application of AI-driven solutions in an enterprise environment.
Demonstrated success defining strategy and delivering scalable dashboards, reporting products, data pipelines, analytics platforms, or AI-enabled experiences using modern tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Databricks, or equivalent technologies.
Proven ability to connect metrics to business strategy and portfolio outcomes, translating operational data into executive-level insights, recommendations, and decision frameworks.
Exceptional communication, visualization, facilitation, and data storytelling skills, with the ability to influence senior audiences and align stakeholders around complex decisions.
Recognized as a trusted advisor and thought leader who collaborates and influences across technical, product, and business stakeholders, aligns diverse perspectives around shared metrics and insights, and delivers results without direct authority.

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

MBA or advanced degree in business, data science, computer science, engineering, or another quantitative discipline.
Background in large-scale technology, product, engineering, or enterprise transformation environments, with experience scaling data-driven decision frameworks and operating models.
Deep knowledge of data science, machine learning, generative AI, responsible AI, and the practical application of these capabilities to enterprise decision-making.
Demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous, enterprise-wide business needs into structured intelligence strategies, governed metrics, scalable reporting systems, and insight-driven products with measurable adoption and impact.

Hybrid or Remote:
This role is categorized as hybrid for those within commutable distance. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to our Engineering Technical Center in Warren (MI) or Austin (TX) three times per week at minimum otherwise open to virtual.

The compensation information is a good faith estimate only. It is based on what a successful applicant might be paid in accordance with applicable state laws. The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of the California Bay Area.

The salary range for this role is $134,700 to $245,00. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.

Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plan, sickness and accident benefits, life insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, employee assistance program, GM vehicle discounts and more.

Who You Are

The Project Manager (PM) supports the Program Manager in planning and executing projects required in the performance of a United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Recurring Maintenance and Minor Repair (RMMR) task order. The PM reports to the Program Manager and is responsible for duties include bidding, planning, organizing, coordinating, monitoring, and administering the work to successfully complete the requirements of the task order on time, within budget and in accordance with the company’s quality, safety, and regulatory requirements. The PM will support project execution throughout its lifecycle; track and coordinate administrative requirements, schedules, and budgets; utilize computerized maintenance systems; ensure clients’ or stakeholders’ requirements are met; process of invoices; manage and guiding project team members when needed.

This position is contingent upon award.

What You’ll Do

Overall responsibility for RMMR activities, goals, and objectives. Leads the project team to complete work on time and within budget.
Provides management and oversight of all requirements of assigned task orders to include project management, safety, quality, and billing.
Facilitates the flow of information between the client and project team in an efficient and timely manner. Provides early notice to client, customer, and staff of revised schedules and project requirements.
Oversees the development of service orders by Project Coordinators. Provides technical oversight of service order scopes of work, ensuring health and safety plans and quality plans are developed and followed. Coordinates with maintenance manager to ensure RM schedules are adhered to and that all tasks are performed in accordance with contract requirements.

Works to ensure adequate resources are assigned and scheduled on projects to meet deadlines and budgets.

interface.ai is redefining how financial institutions serve their members through agentic AI and conversational AI — and we're doing it in production, at scale, with real outcomes. $30M in Series A funding. Build and maintain detailed project schedules, work plans, and milestone trackers that account for customer readiness, third-party integrations, core banking dependencies, and telephony configuration — keeping every stakeholder aligned on what is due and when.

4+ years of project management experience, preferably in financial technology, SaaS implementation, or enterprise software delivery for financial institutions.

Proficiency with project planning tools including Gantt charts, Kanban boards, and project management platforms; able to build and maintain detailed work plans without relying on templates to think.
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills — comfortable running executive status meetings, writing crisp project documentation, and navigating difficult conversations about scope, risk, and timeline.

The Division of Cardiovascular Medicine , Center for Inherited Cardiovascular Disease (SCICD) is one of the largest facilities of its kind in the country. Bachelor's degree or a combination of education and relevant experience.

Experience in a quantitative discipline such as economics, finance, statistics or engineering.

Substantial experience with MS Office and analytical programs.

Ability to prioritize workload.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding an experienced Senior Energy Project Manager
to help expand our energy practice and support a variety of projects from concept through completion in a dynamic consulting environment.

With decades of national experience, Tetra Tech offers extensive technical expertise and a strong understanding of energy development. From planning, siting, evaluation, and permitting through design, construction, operation, and maintenance, Tetra Tech supports clients throughout the energy project lifecycle.

The successful candidate will bring a strong technical background and demonstrated leadership experience supporting energy projects, with an emphasis on commercial-, utility-, and distributed-generation-scale solar photovoltaic (PV), battery energy storage systems (BESS), natural gas power generation, onshore wind, and/or electric transmission projects.

This position will have a significant seller-doer component
, combining project and technical leadership with client development and business growth responsibilities. The successful candidate will develop and strengthen client relationships, identify and pursue new opportunities, and collaborate with Tetra Tech professionals across multiple disciplines to successfully execute energy projects.

The Senior Energy Project Manager will support and provide environmental services throughout project development, design, construction, and operation. Services may include due diligence, project feasibility, natural and cultural resource evaluations, regulatory permitting, environmental studies, compliance support for operating assets, and coordination with engineering teams.

The ideal candidate will have established relationships within the energy market and a demonstrated track record of developing business and winning work. This individual will collaborate with other project managers, environmental leads, account managers, and operational leadership to help establish the strategic direction and continued growth of Tetra Tech’s environmental and energy practice.

This is a full-time, salaried, exempt position and is eligible for hybrid or remote work arrangements.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges.Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world.For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability.Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development.Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference.Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Essential Job Functions

Project & Technical Leadership

Serve as Project Manager or Technical Advisor for complex energy projects.
Manage project scope, schedule, budget, staffing, quality, and overall project performance.
Develop technical approaches, proposals, and cost estimates and direct multidisciplinary project teams.
Lead and manage federal, state, and local permitting processes for complex energy projects.
Provide strategic guidance to clients and project teams in navigating complex project and regulatory challenges.
Oversee teams responsible for environmental planning, permitting, and compliance activities.
Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations and permit requirements.
Collaborate with government agencies, clients, internal technical teams, and external organizations.
Work closely with Operations Managers, Energy Initiative Leads, and Business Unit Leaders to deliver safe, high-quality, profitable, and sustainable projects.
Provide leadership to project teams and promote accountability for project responsibilities, schedules, and milestones.
Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering and engineering design for energy projects, as applicable.

Business Development & Client Leadership

Work with local offices, existing Tetra Tech account managers, operations leaders, and market leads to expand existing client accounts.
Develop, strengthen, and grow relationships with energy clients, including utilities and developers.
Identify and pursue new business opportunities within the energy market.
Participate in client marketing and business development activities, including proposal development, technical presentations, client meetings, trade shows, and development of marketing materials.
Collaborate across the Tetra Tech organization to identify resources and develop multidisciplinary project teams.
Engage with existing and prospective clients to identify new opportunities and expand Tetra Tech’s services.
Support strategic growth of Tetra Tech’s national Energy Practice.
Conduct activities in accordance with company procedures, legislation, and industry standards.
Pursue continuous professional development and maintain a high degree of technical knowledge and industry awareness.
Work safely at all times and report health and safety observations, near misses, and incidents.
Perform additional duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Urban or Regional Planning, Environmental Policy, Environmental Studies, or a related discipline. Graduate degree preferred.
Minimum of 10 years of relevant experience, with additional experience preferred, in energy project development, environmental consulting, business development, environmental assessments, and federal, state, and local regulatory compliance and permitting.
Working knowledge of planning, siting, permitting, design, and construction associated with energy facilities.
Strong working knowledge of state siting and permitting processes.
Demonstrated success managing complex energy or infrastructure projects.
Proven ability to develop client relationships, identify opportunities, and support or lead successful business development efforts.
Demonstrated leadership of multidisciplinary project teams.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously with minimal supervision while effectively prioritizing and meeting deadlines.
Strong leadership, diplomatic, motivational, and team-building skills with the ability to collaborate across multiple business and technical organizations.
Demonstrated ability to work creatively and analytically in a problem-solving environment while promoting teamwork, innovation, and technical excellence.
Experience developing project budgets, proposals, scopes of work, and cost estimates.
Demonstrated success delivering projects on schedule and within budget.
Experience leading and managing internal and external project resources while maintaining accountability for performance.
Strong written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Must possess a valid driver's license with a clean driving record without restrictions.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

jobs.description:
5C DATA CENTERS

Join the Future of Digital Infrastructure

Are you a passionate Technical Project Manager
looking to make a meaningful impact? We're building the next generation of digital infrastructure powering hyperscalers, AI innovation, and high-performance computing across North America.

JOB TITLE

Technical Project Manager,GPU Infrastructure Deployment

DEPARTMENT

Cloud,Ops

LOCATION

USA(Washington, D.C., Phoenix (AZ), Memphis (TN), Columbus (OH), or nearby regions

WORK ARRANGEMENT

Remote

Travel Requirements

Up to 25%

SALARY RANGE

$155K–$175K

Role Summary

We are seeking a Technical Project Manager (TPM) to drive the planning, coordination, and execution of large-scale GPU cluster infrastructure deployment programs. This role partners across multiple engineering teams to manage project schedules, track milestones, resolve blockers, and communicate status across technical teams, datacenter operations, engineering, and external vendors.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Intake & Portfolio Management
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

People Strategy & Enablement (PS&E) bridges the gap between strategy and impact. We create clarity and momentum for People initiatives, partnering cross-functionally to design and run scalable programs and products that improve decisions, reduce friction, and support sustainable growth. By enabling operational excellence and alignment, we ensure the People team can move faster and with confidence.

Our work spans five core areas: strategic planning and roadmap prioritization to ensure the People team focuses on the highest-value initiatives; pillar management to track health, risks, and progress of strategic initiatives with transparency and accountability; project management to provide the discipline and structure required to move initiatives across the finish line — from inception through delivery; design readiness and change management to prepare the organization to adopt and sustain new programs; and People operating rhythms to organize and facilitate planning cadences and forums that keep the organization aligned and moving.

The role

This is not a typical project management role. As Project Manager for People Operations Intake & Portfolio, you will own the systems, processes, and judgment layer that determines what the Partners, Operations & Insights (POI) organization works on — and in what order. You will be the connective tissue between the People team's ambitions and POI's capacity, serving as the first point of contact for all work requests flowing into POI's four core teams: People Solutions, People Data Analytics & Research (PDAR), People Partners, and Employee Relations & HR Compliance.

You will build and run Stripe's POI intake and prioritization process end-to-end — from designing the intake experience for requestors, to triaging and evaluating incoming Jira tickets, to facilitating prioritization conversations with POI and People team leaders. As this function matures, you will expand into a broader portfolio intelligence role: the key strategic partner to all People team requestors, ensuring that the organization's most limited resource — team capacity — is always directed at the highest-priority work.

Critically, you will also build an AI agent to power and scale this work. You will design, iterate on, and deploy an intelligent intake assistant that helps with automated scoping, duplicate request detection, time commitment estimation, resourcing recommendations, and prioritization guidance — upleveling the quality of every intake interaction across the org.

What you'll do

Own and operate the POI intake process end-to-end. Manage the Jira-based intake system, ensuring all incoming requests are triaged promptly, routed correctly, and tracked through their full lifecycle from submission to delivery.
Serve as the primary intake partner for People team requestors. Act as a knowledgeable, approachable first point of contact who helps teams scope and frame requests well, setting clear expectations on timelines, effort, and likelihood of prioritization.
Facilitate regular intake and portfolio cadences. Set cadence for POI Intake reviews, backlog grooming, and full roadmap reviews.
Identify systemic patterns and surface insights to leadership. Synthesize trends across intake submissions to proactively flag capacity constraints, recurring themes, capability gaps, and emerging risks before they become blockers..
Apply strategic judgment to prioritize the POI portfolio. Evaluate incoming tickets against People team SOKRs, the 3-Year Plan (3YP), and establish prioritization frameworks.
Build and maintain portfolio visibility and capacity reporting. Develop dashboards and reporting that give POI leadership and People team stakeholders real-time insight into resource allocation, queue depth, and roadmap health. Participate in quarterly business reviews and annual planning cycles.
Design, build, and continuously improve an AI agent for intake. Create an intelligent agent that automates and enhances the intake experience, that ultimately can be deployed to reduce time-to-decision and improve requestor experience at scale.
Continuously improve the intake experience. Build and maintain requestor-facing documentation, submission guides, communication templates, and onboarding materials that reduce friction and improve ticket quality at submission.
Partner with POI leaders and People team leaders on resourcing and prioritization conversations. Prepare and present portfolio data and recommendations to senior stakeholders, facilitating trade-off discussions with rigor, objectivity, and a clear point of view.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, we encourage you to apply. Preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of experience in project management, business operations, strategy, or consulting with experience navigating complex, matrixed organizations and managing competing priorities.
Demonstrated experience designing, building, or significantly improving an intake, triage, or portfolio management process for a delivery team or operations function.
Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills. Able to evaluate competing requests against strategic frameworks, make well-reasoned prioritization recommendations, and communicate trade-offs clearly to senior stakeholders.
Proficiency in Jira or equivalent ticketing/project management tools. Comfortable with workflow configuration, ticket lifecycle management, capacity planning, and reporting.
Proven experience using AI tools (LLMs, AI agents, or automation platforms) to streamline workflows, build lightweight productivity solutions, or automate repetitive operational tasks.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Able to translate ambiguous, incomplete requests into clear, actionable project briefs and present complex portfolio data accessibly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Proven ability to manage relationships with senior stakeholders (directors, VPs), including setting expectations, navigating pushback, and facilitating alignment conversations with confidence.
Comfort operating in ambiguous environments where the work is not always well-defined. Able to independently identify the right approach and establish meaningful success metrics.
Collaborative, low-ego working style. Able to operate as a strategic partner and trusted advisor rather than a decision-maker, earning credibility through rigor and good judgment.
At least 2 years of experience working within or closely alongside an HR, People, or equivalent internal operations team.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience building AI agents or automation workflows using no-code/low-code tooling.
Experience with prompt engineering, RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) concepts, or designing human-in-the-loop workflows for AI-assisted processes.
Background in portfolio management, demand management, or capacity planning, including experience with prioritization frameworks (RICE, WSJF, OKR-alignment scoring, or similar).
Experience with change management frameworks (e.g., Prosci ADKAR® Model) and designing adoption strategies for new processes or tooling.
Familiarity with HR systems (e.g., Workday, Greenhouse, Retool) and People team workflows.
Experience building portfolio dashboards or capacity reports using tools like Tableau, Looker, Google Sheets, or similar.
Experience building and deploying process documentation, requestor-facing guides, or enablement materials that improve submission quality and reduce intake friction.
Familiarity with data privacy and compliance considerations relevant to employee data, particularly in the context of AI tools and automated workflows.
Experience using AI tools to increase personal and team productivity.
Advanced proficiency in Google Workspace (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and Mac OS.

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

jobs.title: Program Manager, Performance and Talent Planning
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a significant amount of work ahead. That means you have an opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Performance and Talent Planning team is part of Stripe’s broader Talent and Development organization. We shape how Stripes grow their careers and do their best work.

We build the programs, systems, and insights that help managers develop strong teams, help leaders plan for the future, and give Stripes clear opportunities to grow. Our work spans performance, talent planning, career development, succession, and organizational insights. Our goal is to make Stripe a place where talented people can build lasting careers and have an outsized impact.

What you’ll do

In this role, you will help translate Stripe’s performance and talent philosophy into scalable, global experiences. You will work across People Products, People Insights, Employee Relations, People Partners and other partner teams to design programs and systems that are clear for users, operationally durable, and aligned with Stripe’s future needs. You will bring a product mindset to all you do, starting with data driven problem statements, qualitative and quantitative signals, an understanding of the end-to-end user experience, an iterative design process, and an obsession with continuous improvement over time. You will be comfortable operating across time zones and navigating competing perspectives, incomplete information, and urgent priorities.

A Day in the Life

You start your day by reviewing your agenda in Slack or asking your AI agent to summarize ongoing work and priorities. Energized by a mix of workstream meetings across People Products, Manager Enablement, and M&A Transitions, you check overnight updates from teammates across time zones. Colleagues in Dublin have shared feedback that keeps the launch plan moving, while teammates in Melbourne have raised thoughtful questions about how a new performance process will integrate into the existing reporting capabilities they rely on for annual talent planning.

These questions are exactly the kind of challenge you value. They push you to build with a user-first mindset, anticipate downstream impacts, and mitigate risks before they emerge. You draw on expertise from across the organization while balancing the responsibility of integrating global perspectives, designing seamless end-to-end experiences, and coordinating work across interconnected teams. A new question sparks a new connection, and you quickly identify another stakeholder who should be brought into the next phase of the program.

As the day progresses, updates from cross-functional partners show steady progress across multiple fronts, but one critical area stalls. Rather than waiting for next week's meeting, you escalate immediately to keep momentum high and de-risk the program timeline. You end the day energized by the complexity of the work, the curiosity and collaboration of your colleagues, and the opportunity to continue to build, solve, and innovate every day.

Responsibilities

Drive and scale Stripe’s performance philosophy and practices. Design and improve performance experiences that help Stripes understand expectations, grow through feedback, and make meaningful contributions.
Evolve performance and talent tooling. Partner with People Products and cross-functional stakeholders to translate program needs into scalable systems, processes, and user journeys.
Strengthen career growth and talent investment. Help shape the programs, mechanisms, and insights that enable career development, talent planning, succession, and thoughtful investment in Stripe’s people as the company grows.
Lead complex, cross-functional workstreams. Build alignment among global stakeholders; surface risks and dependencies early; make progress in ambiguous environments; and unblock critical decisions quickly.
Use insights to improve outcomes. Define clear problem statements, gather qualitative and quantitative data, and use those insights to refine strategy, programs, and execution.

Who you are

You are a systems thinker who can connect the details of a program or product experience to the broader organizational context. You are energized by ambiguity and complexity, and thrive in bringing just enough structure, clarity, and strong momentum to the work. You build trusted relationships, communicate directly and thoughtfully, and create accountability across teams, with speed.

Minimum Requirements

10+ years of experience building and scaling global People or HR experiences, with experience across both process and product or systems design
Experience leading complex programs in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where high ownership and cross-functional problem solving are expected.
Strong systems thinking: the ability to understand how people, processes, tools, policies, and organizational decisions influence one another over time and how to augment workflows and processes using AI tools.
A demonstrated ability to build enduring, trusted stakeholder relationships; communicate effectively across levels and functions; and establish clear decision-making and accountability mechanisms.
A disciplined approach to problem solving. You begin with the “why,” define and refine problem statements steeped in both quantitative and qualitative data, and continuously ask “is this the right problem to solve, at the right time?”
High agency and sound judgment. You identify opportunities or risks, take action quickly, and escalate thoughtfully when progress is blocked.
Deep alignment with Stripe’s Operating Principle, Obsess over Talent. You believe that people are one of Stripe’s greatest unlocks: attracting exceptional talent, creating environments where they can thrive, building systems that support growth, and recognizing meaningful contributions.
Curiosity and humility. You are a continuous learner who seeks to understand before acting, welcomes ideas from many sources, and is willing to change course when new evidence suggests a better path.

Preferred Qualifications

10+ years of experience across a diverse portfolio of People programs: talent management, organizational development, leadership and/or executive development, program and talent operations, and compensation and benefits
People product design and management experience in high growth environments with fast iterative cycles, changing priorities, and a steady stream of feature requests and backlog
Experience and excellence leading executive level talent discussions that influence People strategy, with humility, curiosity, and a grounded presence

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $129,400 - $194,200. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

At Equinix, talent is a strategic differentiator. As the Program Manager, Global Emerging Talent, you will help shape the workforce of the future by designing and delivering innovative talent solutions that build critical capabilities, accelerate business outcomes, and strengthen long-term talent pipelines.

Reporting Equinix’s Integrated Talent Solutions (ITS), you will serve as a Strategic Talent Advisor and Program Owner, partnering with business leaders, HR, and talent stakeholders to align emerging talent strategies with workforce priorities and future skills needs.

Through a deep understanding of business demand, talent supply, and market dynamics, you will help leaders navigate talent decisions and create pathways that unlock opportunity, build organizational capability, and enable sustainable growth. Leveraging Talent Intelligence, Talent Marketplace capabilities, and Build-Borrow-Buy-Place principles, you will lead the strategy, execution, and evolution of global internship, apprenticeship, and trainee programs that strengthen Equinix's talent ecosystem and deliver measurable business impact.

This role is ideal for a leader who thrives at the intersection of workforce strategy, talent innovation, program execution, and organizational transformation.

Responsibilities

Strategic Talent Advisory

Serve as a trusted advisor to business leaders, HR, and Functional Partner Teams, translating workforce demand into innovative talent solutions
Partner with leaders to identify future capability needs and determine how emerging talent programs can accelerate workforce readiness and business growth
Advise on workforce strategies using Build-Borrow-Buy-Place principles, helping leaders balance immediate hiring needs with long-term capability development
Leverage talent intelligence, labor market insights, and workforce data to inform decision-making, talent planning, and investment priorities
Influence talent decisions through a skills-based lens, ensuring alignment between business objectives and future workforce requirements

Global Emerging Talent Strategy

Develop and execute the global strategy for internships, apprenticeships, traineeships, and other emerging talent pathways
Identify opportunities to expand and modernize talent pipelines to meet evolving business and skills demands
Create scalable frameworks, governance models, and operating rhythms that enable consistent global delivery while supporting regional requirements
Drive continuous innovation in how Equinix attracts, develops, and converts emerging talent into future organizational capability

Program Leadership & Delivery

Own the end-to-end lifecycle of global emerging talent programs, from strategy and planning through execution, measurement, and continuous improvement
Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives involving HR, Talent Acquisition, Talent Marketplace, HR Operations, Finance, Communications, Legal, and business stakeholders
Establish success metrics, reporting frameworks, and dashboards that demonstrate program effectiveness, talent outcomes, and business value
Ensure programs are delivered with operational excellence, within budget, on schedule, and aligned with strategic objectives

Talent Marketplace & Skills-Based Talent Solutions

Partner closely with Talent Marketplace and workforce planning stakeholders to integrate emerging talent pathways into broader talent strategies
Enable skills-based talent practices by connecting program design to future capabilities, workforce priorities, and business outcomes
Create pathways that support long-term career growth, internal mobility, and workforce sustainability
Identify opportunities to connect emerging talent initiatives with enterprise transformation and workforce planning efforts

Stakeholder Engagement & Influence

Build trusted partnerships with leaders across the business, Human Resources, and Integrated Talent Solutions
Influence decision-making by translating complex workforce challenges into clear, actionable talent strategies
Deliver compelling executive communications, recommendations, and presentations to senior leaders and governance forums
Act as a visible advocate for emerging talent, workforce innovation, and skills-based talent strategies across the enterprise

Change Leadership

Lead change initiatives associated with talent transformation and workforce innovation efforts
Develop stakeholder engagement, communication, and adoption strategies that drive successful implementation and sustainable outcomes
Foster alignment across global teams and create momentum around new ways of building and developing talent

What Success Looks Like

Emerging talent programs are recognized as strategic workforce solutions that deliver measurable business outcomes
Leaders view Emerging Talent as a trusted partner in workforce planning and capability-building conversations
Talent pipelines are aligned to future skill needs and business priorities
Program participants successfully transition into high-impact roles that strengthen organizational capability
Data, talent intelligence, and workforce insights consistently inform decisions and investment strategies
The programs contribute meaningfully to Equinix's workforce of the future strategy and culture of continuous learning

Qualifications

Required

7+ years of experience leading enterprise-wide programs, workforce initiatives, or talent strategies in Human Resources, Talent Acquisition, Workforce Planning, Talent Management, or related functions
Demonstrated success partnering with senior leaders to influence strategy, drive change, and deliver business outcomes
Experience managing complex, global, cross-functional programs and organizational initiatives
Strong program management, stakeholder management, and change leadership capabilities
Excellent executive communication, facilitation, and consulting skills
Ability to translate workforce challenges into scalable talent solutions
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience

Preferred

Experience building, scaling, or optimizing internship, apprenticeship, trainee, or other emerging talent programs
Experience with Talent Marketplace, workforce planning, talent intelligence, talent mobility, or skills-based workforce practices
Knowledge of Build-Borrow-Buy-Place and strategic workforce planning methodologies
Experience operating within complex, global organizations undergoing transformation
Program, project management, agile, or change management certifications

Why Join Us

This role is an opportunity to influence how Equinix builds the workforce of tomorrow. You will help shape talent strategies that create access to opportunity, strengthen critical capabilities, and enable the business to thrive in a rapidly evolving world. You won't simply manage talent programs. You'll help design the future talent ecosystem of Equinix, creating pathways that connect people, skills, and business opportunity at a global scale.

jobs.title: Security Program Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Security Program Manager

Security Services, Cybersecurity & Compliance

We are Lennar

Lennar is one of the nation's leading homebuilders, dedicated to making an impact and creating an extraordinary experience for their Homeowners, Communities, and Associates by building quality homes and providing exceptional customer service, giving back to the communities in which we work and live in, and fostering a culture of opportunity and growth for our Associates throughout their career. Lennar has been recognized as a Fortune 500® company and consistently ranked among the top homebuilders in the United States.

A Career that Empowers You to Build Your Future

Lennar has an opportunity for a Security Program Manager within the Resilience and Security Services organization, working in close partnership with Security, primarily comprised of Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) and Privacy, to run the enterprise program that keeps Lennar's NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) controls backed by clear, current policy and verifiable evidence of adherence. This role reports directly to the Director, Resilience and Security Services.

The Security Program Manager is Lennar's primary point of contact for internal and external audit engagements and regulatory inquiries, and the trusted advisor to the federation of control owners across Lennar IT (LTG) who author and maintain policy. This is a program management role at its core: the Security Program Manager runs the assurance program end-to-end, setting the annual cadence, managing cross-functional workstreams, and holding every deliverable, policy review, evidence request, and audit response to a disciplined program plan. Additional insight into cybersecurity and IT auditing is a major plus.

A career with purpose.
A career built on making dreams come true.
A career built on building zero defect homes, cost management, and adherence to schedules.

Your Responsibilities On The Team

Lead and manage the enterprise assurance program as a structured, multi-workstream initiative, applying disciplined program and project management practices (Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid, as appropriate) to keep every deliverable on time and within scope.
Build and maintain the year-long assurance calendar, aligning evidence-gathering activity, policy reviews, and audit response with Lennar's regulatory and audit calendars.
Own the enterprise policy library: maintain an accurate, current inventory of every policy tied to an enforced NIST CSF control, manage the policy lifecycle on an annual review cadence, and read every policy closely for clarity, completeness, and fidelity to the intent of the underlying control.
Design and maintain the standard process flow that governs how a policy moves from draft through review, giving control owners a clear, repeatable path to a compliant policy. Security retains final review and sign-off authority on every policy; the Security Program Manager ensures the process is followed.
Own the evidence library: ensure evidence is properly cataloged, stored, and retrievable, and that evidence approaching the end of its one-year validity window is refreshed before it expires.
Serve as Lennar's primary liaison to internal and external audit teams and regulatory bodies, leading the response to audit and regulatory evidence requests with a service-oriented, no-surprises approach, and reusing previously validated evidence wherever it falls within its one-year validity period.
Partner directly with control and policy owners across the LTG federation, providing patient, constructive guidance and facilitating solution-oriented working sessions that keep policy work moving ahead of Security's final review.
Lead the evaluation and selection of the system(s) of record for the policy and evidence libraries, anticipated to be a combination of SharePoint and AuditBoard, with final tooling to be determined as an initial program deliverable.
Identify and help assess security and compliance risks surfacing from policy gaps, control weaknesses, or stale evidence, applying working knowledge of relevant frameworks (NIST CSF, SOC, PCI, FFIEC) to escalate substantive issues to Security and the Director, Resilience and Security Services.
Communicate program status, risks, and issues to stakeholders and senior management, including VP/SVP-level leadership, in clear, concise, executive-ready formats.
Mentor and guide program contributors, including a proposed Security Analyst II role should it be approved, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and disciplined execution.
Analyze multi-domain assurance trend data, including audit findings, evidence turnaround, and policy currency, to institutionalize process fixes and improve reliability at scale.
Maintain the assurance program's source of truth in Lennar's management platforms, ensuring all artifacts meet global security and audit control standards.
Define program requirements by managing milestones, forming working teams with control owners, and establishing budgets where applicable; monitor progress by tracking activity, resolving problems, and publishing progress reports.

Requirements

7+ years of professional experience spanning IT project/program management, audit, risk, compliance, or governance, including at least 5 years leading multi-workstream projects or programs.
Proven program/project management discipline: experience with Agile (Scrum, XP), Waterfall/Predictive, and hybrid methodologies; PMP certification preferred.
Extremely detail-oriented and hyper-organized, comfortable owning a portfolio of concurrent, time-sensitive deliverables (policy reviews, evidence requests, audit responses) without dropping a thread.
Experience interacting with internal or external audit teams, with a service-oriented mindset and the presence to represent Lennar credibly in audit and regulatory conversations.
Demonstrated ability to read, interpret, and translate the intent of a policy into practical guidance for control owners; collaborative and personable enough to coach non-compliance professionals through it.
Working knowledge of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) and NIST SP 800-53 control families, or a comparable enterprise control framework; familiarity with SOC, PCI, and FFIEC compliance requirements is a strong plus.
Additional insight into cybersecurity and IT auditing, including security risk and vulnerability identification, is a major plus.
Experience selecting, implementing, or administering Security and document management platforms; direct experience with AuditBoard and SharePoint preferred.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with an emphasis on facilitating solution-oriented meetings and briefing VP/SVP-level stakeholders on status, risk, and trade-offs.
Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Systems, Risk Management, or a related field; Master's degree preferred, or equivalent experience.
Certifications a plus: PMP, CISA, CRISC, CIA, CGEIT, CISSP, or equivalent.

Physical & Office/Site Presence Requirements:

Regular, in-person attendance at the Lennar office during regular work hours is an essential function of this job. This is primarily a sedentary office position which requires the incumbent to have the ability to operate computer equipment, speak, hear, bend, stoop, reach, lift, and move and carry up to 25 lbs. Finger dexterity is necessary.

This description outlines the basic responsibilities and requirements for the position noted. This is not a comprehensive listing of all job duties of the Associates. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Life at Lennar

At Lennar, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching environment for our Associates, offering a comprehensive array of benefits designed to enhance their well-being and professional growth. Our Associates have access to robust health insurance plans, including Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage, ensuring their health needs are well taken care of. Our 401(k) Retirement Plan, complete with a $1 for $1 Company Match up to 5%, helps secure their financial future, while Paid Parental Leave and an Associate Assistance Plan provide essential support during life's critical moments. To further support our Associates, we provide an Education Assistance Program and up to $30,000 in Adoption Assistance, underscoring our commitment to their diverse needs and aspirations. From the moment of hire, they can enjoy up to three weeks of vacation annually, alongside generous Holiday, Sick Leave, and Personal Day policies. Additionally, we offer a New Hire Referral Bonus Program, significant Home Purchase Discounts, and unique opportunities such as the Everyone’s Included Day. At Lennar, we believe in investing in our Associates, empowering them to thrive both personally and professionally. Lennar Associates will have access to these benefits as outlined by Lennar’s policies and applicable plan terms. Visit Lennartotalrewards.com to view our suite of benefits.

Join the fun and follow us on social media to see what's happening at our company, and don't forget to connect with us on Lennar: Overview | LinkedIn<https://www.linkedin.com/company/lennar/> for the latest job opportunities.

Lennar is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws.

The position will work across functions to align vision, scope, and strategic business objectives, while translating ambiguity into clear, data-driven plans with measurable milestones. The role entails facilitating critical trade-off decisions, proactively surfacing and mitigating risks, preparing leaders for high-impact phase gate decisions, and actively managing the project budget through forecasting, tracking actuals, and course-correcting as needed. How You’ll Make An Impact

Lead a cross-functional team to develop new products from initiation through commercial launch, with the goal of delivering high-quality outcomes within agreed-upon schedule, resources, budget, and scope. Ensure alignment across product value proposition, project scope, and strategic business objectives.
Lead development and execution of projects by working cross-functionally to create and execute project plans, managing project resource in partnership with functional leaders, and managing project risks in collaboration with core teams.
Lead core team and project decision making by leading team assessments of options and trade-offs (such as balancing customer value, budget, resources, and business case), leading team preparations for Phase Gate and other Go/No-Go decisions by executive leadership, and actively managing project stakeholder needs, communications, and engagement.
